report.summary: The game's deathmatch is a plain UWorld whose WorldSettings set the game mode, plus a set of data assets. /Game/OnlineMode/Maps/DM/PL_DM_001, 002, 003, 004 and 006 set LiveWorldSettings.DefaultGameMode = BP_ChronicleDeathMatchGameMode and MissionSettings.MissionConfig = MC_DM, and all five share WD_DM, EP_DM (reached through the game mode's GameModeEvents), IS_DM_000 and DT_Rdo_DM. The class chain is ALiveDeathMatchGameMode < ALiveSoloPVPGameMode < ALiveOnlineGameMode < ALiveGameMode < AGameMode, all with no reflected UFUNCTIONs except ALiveGameMode's replay handlers. The GameState is the empty ALiveGameState. No UE replication is used: sync runs through the GameInstance's Strix and network managers. As data, a DM match is: 8 single-pilot factions (Alpha to Zulu), each with 1 start and 5 selectable respawn points; a 35 x 35 x 40 km combat zone; no NPCs and no bots. MC_DM gives MissionLimitTime 210 s and VictoryScore 500000. DT_MissionContents row 16 gives BaseRespawnTime 10, ConnectionsLeftNum 1 and MissionSuccessSeconds 105. Score counts player damage, player kills and indirect kills, scaled by the aircraft-cost tables. The hourly schedule rotates three DM maps and applies no special rule (no cost or role limit). In the exe, DM ends when any player's score reaches the config's VictoryScore (finish byte GameMode+0x538 = 3) or on time-up (=2) or forced termination (=4), then calls vfunc +0xab8. Because 500000 is far above any kill score, the match ends in practice by Timeup, which matches EP_DM's DM_MissionFinish_* triggers (Timeup plus rank 1 to 8). At run time the game looks up the current mode type through the InformationManager's mission map, keyed by a mission ID that the GameInstance holds. Opening PL_DM_00x with OpenLevel without setting that ID would leave the mode type wrong. The online game mode's sync points (MissionEndSyncTick, OnGameFinish, BeginGameTermination) go through GameInstance+0x910 (StrixManager_), +0x928 (NetworkManager_) and the local plane's ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane. Some of those paths are null- or flag-guarded, but whether the ELiveOnlineGameModeState machine (WaitingNetworkInitialize → TimeSync → SyncStartMatch → GamePlaying) gets past its waits offline with no Strix room cannot be settled statically. Part of the code is virtualized (the online constructor jumps into .sbss). For RVNG, the native path is to load a PL_DM_00x map with the current mission ID set to a DM row (1600x0) so its own BP_ChronicleDeathMatchGameMode, MC_DM, WD_DM and score/respawn tables run. RVNG would then express its rules through MC_DM (time and VictoryScore) and DT_MissionContents semantics rather than its own timers. Its P2P link has to stand in for what the Strix room and NetworkManager provide (room members, time sync, start and end sync, forced termination). Whether the online game mode can be driven offline at all is the first in-game test.

findings.topic: How the running game knows the mode type (mission-ID routing)
findings.finding: Online game-mode code asks 0x147ec9d20(ctx) for the current ELiveGameModeType. That function reads the current MissionID from *(GameInstance+0x8e0)+0xf38 (0x147ec9cc0), then looks it up in the InformationManager (GameInstance+0x878) mission map (0x14734cac0, a TMap<int32 MissionID, FLiveLevelTable>, element stride 0x818). MissionEndSyncTick and OnGameFinish skip their network sync when that type is 10 or 11 (OnlineTutorials, OnlineFreeFlight: `sub al,0xa; cmp al,1; jbe`). The InformationManager at +0x878 and NetworkManager_ at +0x928 match the Survival docs. From member order, +0x8e0 = UserDataManager_, +0x910 = StrixManager_ (0x1474ae240 returns GI+0x910), +0x938 = NetworkCheatManager_ and +0x958 = MissionRoomMemberManager_ (inferred). Consequence: OpenLevel of PL_DM_00x by path does not change that mission ID, so mode-type-dependent code (sync skips, HUD per-mode widget, damage-rate table choice, score rules) would see the previous mission's type unless the ID is set to 1600x0 first.

findings.topic: How a DM match ends (native finish logic)
findings.finding: GameMode+0x538 holds ELiveFinishConditionType. 0x1471c93c0 (online generic time-up) sets it to 2 (Timeup) and jumps to vtable +0xab8 (slot 343). DM's override at slot 360 (0x1471df5c0, body 0x1471df5f0..0x1471df73b) gets the DM mission config (IsA check, fallback to the CDO). For each player it calls 0x147d19600 to get a float score and compares it with float(config+0x200 VictoryScore). When score ≥ VictoryScore it sets +0x538 = 3 (VictoryScore) and calls vfunc +0xab8. Network forced termination near RecvPreparingMissionEnd (0x1471cba7a) sets it to 4. The TDM equivalent at 0x1471e0e2e..0x1471e0f0c compares two team scores from 0x1471c9a90(this, team 1 or 2) with the TDM config's VictoryScore. Slot 343 (+0xab8) is overridden by DM (0x1471df1f0, vs SoloPVP 0x1471e0970). A kill pays roughly victim BaseScore 1400-4000 (DT_PlayerAircraftCost) × rate 1.0, so 500000 cannot be reached in 210 s. DM therefore ends by Timeup, matching EP_DM's DM_MissionFinish triggers, which carry Value=Timeup and a rank 1..8 (or 0 = NoRank).

findings.topic: Respawn rule
findings.finding: The base respawn time is 10 s, from both the ALiveGameMode ctor (BaseRespawnTime @0x3d0 = 10.0, not overridden by the DM BP) and DT_MissionContents.BaseRespawnTime=10. It is scaled per aircraft by DT_PlayerAircraftCost.RespawnRate, which runs from 0.4 at CostTotal 0 to 2.0 at CostTotal ≥4400 (e.g. 1.1 at 1200, 1.4 at 1700). Parts can modify it through EPartsParameterList::RespawnTime / RespawnTime_Team / RespawnTime_Rescue. The pilot chooses one of the faction's respawn points (bCanChaoice; ULiveNUIRespawnPointWidget). The pause/respawn widget ULiveNUIInGamePauseRespawnWidget has an AutomaticRespawnTime (auto-confirm). Respawn completion is the reflected ALivePlayerPlane.OnRespawnFinish delegate, and online sync uses the Strix message FLiveMessageRespawnTimeEnd. The exact formula (base × rate × parts) is inferred from the table names.

findings.finding: In DT_GameModeScoreCalculationTable the Deathmatch row enables only bCalcPlayerDamageScore, bCalcPlayerKillScore, bCalcIndirectKillScore and bCalcOverallScoreRank: no NPC score, assist, decoy, electronic-measure or threat-level score. findings.topic: What the online game mode touches at its network sync points (offline risk)
findings.finding: 0x1471c8190 (MissionEndSyncTick, vtable slot 426) gets the GI, then X = GI+0x928 (NetworkManager_). If the mode type is not 10 or 11, the termination phase field this+0x80c == 0, and 0x1474b3860(X) returns true, it calls 0x1471cb5e0(this, byte+0x729, byte+0x72a, FString 'ALiveOnlineGameMode::MissionEndSyncTick'). 0x1474b3860 goes through GI+0x910 (StrixManager_) and its +0x520 id into a global Strix-side map at 0x14e4c5818 that is null-checked. It then clears NetworkManager+0x718 bit 12 and +0x710, and compares this+0x3cc (or a value from 0x1471d17f0()+0xd8) with this+0x57c. 0x1471cb5e0 (BeginGameTermination) runs only when +0x80c < 1. It sends 0x1474c69c0(localPlane.NetworkObject@+0xed0 as ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane, a, b), sets +0x80c = 1, and if StrixManager+0x1fa is set computes NetworkManager+0x624 from an InformationManager lookup. OnGameFinish (0x1471c9653..) calls into GI+0x938, uses StrixManager+0x1fa / NetworkManager+0x4c0/+0x520, calls the GameMode's NetworkObject (+0x738) 0x1474a64d0, and runs the same named sync. So the online flow is wired to the Strix and network managers and to the room. Many paths are guarded by IsA, null or flag checks, which suggests they degrade to no-ops without a room, but none of this has been run offline. The DebugPIESettings (ConnectServer, NumberOfDummyPlayers, bFactionDeathMatchFromFirstData) show the developers ran online modes against a server even in PIE.
sources: E:/ACE8 Survival Mode/docs/re/COOP.md:178-205 (remote spawn reads session/room player data)

findings.topic: Do /Game/OnlineMode assets load in an offline session
findings.finding: All DM assets are cooked in pakchunk20 (Live/Content/OnlineMode/...). Survival Mode, which only plays offline campaign maps, loads /Game/OnlineMode Niagara effects and camera shakes at run time (Helios blast NS_ms17supsExplosion01_ON, Alicorn discharge effects, BP_CamShake_HandShake_A). The DM map, MC_DM, WD_DM and the BP game mode are therefore present on every install and loadable offline as assets. ChronInformationSettings.OnlineMissionDataTable is a hard UDataTable* member of the GameInstance's InformationSettings, so the online mission rows (DM 1600x0) are loaded even offline. That last point is inferred from the hard reference.

rvngImplications: Use the game's own DM content as-is: open one of /Game/OnlineMode/Maps/DM/PL_DM_001|002|003|004|006. Its WorldSettings already select BP_ChronicleDeathMatchGameMode, MC_DM, WD_DM, EP_DM, IS_DM_000 and DT_Rdo_DM. Do not build a parallel map, game mode or rule set.

Before travelling, make the game believe the current mission is a DM row (MissionID 160010/160020/160030/160040/160060). The mode type is resolved from the InformationManager's FLiveLevelTable by the GameInstance's current MissionID (*(GI+0x8e0)+0xf38 in this build). Prefer the game's own mission-ID travel (MapChangeManager/UserDataManager path) over a raw OpenLevel, which would leave GameModeType at the previous mission's value.

For a 1v1, give the two pilots opposite DM factions, e.g. Alpha (start 0,-7500) and Lima (start 0,7500), 15 km apart, each with its own 5 respawn points. These are the factions the native start/respawn assignment and the team-intro IGC already understand.

Express RVNG's rules through the native config, not Lua timers. The time limit is ULiveDeathMatchMissionConfig.MissionLimitTime (config+0x30, 210 s by default) and the score cap is VictoryScore (config+0x200, 500000). Set them on MC_DM, or on GameMode.MissionConfig @0x530 before the match starts. The native victory is score-based (player score ≥ VictoryScore), not kill-count-based. A 'first to N kills' rule would need either an equivalent VictoryScore (approximate, because damage score counts too) or a native kill counter, so say so in the rules.

Read the outcome from the game rather than inferring it. The finish reason is GameMode+0x538 (ELiveFinishConditionType: 2 Timeup, 3 VictoryScore, 4 ForcedTermination). Ranking is ALiveDeathMatchGameMode.RankingForPlayers @0x830, and the player's score comes from the score getter 0x147d19600. EP_DM's DM_MissionFinish_<rank> triggers fire at time-up. There are no reflected UFUNCTIONs for match start or end, so RVNG's HOOKS.MatchStart/MatchEnd need native hooks (e.g. vtable slot 343 at +0xab8 for the finish, and the online state handlers) or polling of those fields.

Disconnects should follow the game's own forced-end rule. The DT_MissionContents DM row says ConnectionsLeftNum=1 and MissionSuccessSeconds=105, i.e. force-end when only one connection is left, and count it as finished only after 105 s. RVNG's P2P link should feed 'opponent gone' into the native ForcedTermination path (+0x538 = 4 via the RecvPreparingMissionEnd logic) instead of a mod-side surrender rule.

Respawn is native: 10 s base (BaseRespawnTime / DT_MissionContents), scaled by DT_PlayerAircraftCost.RespawnRate for the aircraft's cost and by parts. The pilot chooses one of the faction's Respawn_A..E points through the in-game respawn widget. RVNG only needs to sync that the remote plane respawned (the game's Respawn*/RespawnTimeEnd messages), not to re-implement timing.

Damage, score and loadouts should come from the online tables: DT_CategoryDamageRateForPlayerDataTable_ON, DT_GameModeScoreCalculationTable 'Deathmatch' (player damage, player kill and indirect kill only), DT_ScoreConstTable, the aircraft-cost BaseScore, and airsets with no SpecialRule (DM has no cost or role limit). Confirm in game that these are the tables actually selected when the mode type is Deathmatch.

RVNG's P2P link has to stand in for what the Strix room provides to ALiveOnlineGameMode. That means the room member list (MissionRoomMemberManager GI+0x958 and its aircraft selectors), the local/remote network objects (ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane on each plane, ULiveNetworkGameMode at GameMode+0x738), the sync points (SyncStartMatchTick, MissionEndSyncTick, RecvPreparingMissionEnd) and time sync. The online state machine waits on those. If the native online game mode cannot be made to progress offline, the fallback that still uses the game's data is: keep the DM map, MC_DM, WD_DM and tables, but run it under ?game= with an offline game mode and replicate only the start/finish triggers. That is a compromise and should be decided only after the in-game test.
There are no bots (AllowBot=false) and no NPC units in WD_DM, so the AI-spawn states (SpawnAIs/WaitingSpawnedAIs) should have nothing to wait for in DM.
blockers: It is unknown whether ALiveOnlineGameMode's state machine (WaitingNetworkInitialize → PostNetworkInitialize → LoadPlayerPlane → SpawnPlayerPlane → TimeSync → ... → SyncStartMatch → GamePlaying) gets past its waits offline without a Strix room. Its constructor and parts of its code jump into protected or virtualized code (0x146f807c0 → 0x15a915b50), which limits static RE.

Player planes in the online flow are spawned from room/session data (MissionRoomMemberManager at GI+0x958, aircraft selectors, the remote-spawn path described in docs/re/COOP.md §6). Offline there is no room, so the local plane may never spawn in LoadPlayerPlane/SpawnPlayerPlane.
No DM-specific network class exists (only the base ULiveNetworkGameMode). Everything DM-specific that crosses the network rides on generic online messages that RVNG's link must reproduce.

The current-mission-ID field used for mode routing (*(GI+0x8e0)+0xf38) and the GI member offsets are derived from code reads plus member-order arithmetic. They must be confirmed with UE4SS before RVNG writes them.
The forced-end struct FLiveMissionForcedEndRuleDataTableRow has no shipped DataTable. The live rules are in DT_MissionContents and the native code that applies them was not traced.
openQuestions: Offline DM boot test: at the main menu (UE4SS), read GI+0x8e0→+0xf38, set it to 160010, then OpenLevel('/Game/OnlineMode/Maps/DM/PL_DM_001'). Log the spawned GameMode class (expect BP_ChronicleDeathMatchGameMode_C) and poll its +0x538, +0x80c, +0x729/+0x72a bytes and any byte that walks through 1..19 (the ELiveOnlineGameModeState field). Record whether a player plane spawns and where (expect a Start_<Faction>0 point at 3500 m).
Same test with the mission ID left unset: does the HUD show the DM info widget or the campaign one? That proves whether routing really uses the mission ID.
Override test: OpenLevel PL_DM_001 with '?game=/Script/Live.LiveOfflineGameMode' (and separately with BP_LiveGameMode). Does the map load, use WD_DM starts and respawn points, and run MC_DM's timer?
Timer test: in a running DM, read GameMode.MissionConfig(@0x530)+0x30. Does the HUD count down 210 s or 300 s? This settles the 'passed_4min' radio line.

Finish test: set MissionConfig+0x30 to a small value, let it expire, and confirm +0x538 becomes 2 (Timeup), vfunc +0xab8 runs, EP_DM's DM_MissionFinish_<rank> fires, and the game travels to /Game/OnlineMode/Maps/Menu/Result. Separately set VictoryScore (+0x200) to 1 and confirm +0x538 becomes 3 on the first damage or kill.

Respawn test: die in a DM with a plane of known cost. Measure the respawn delay against 10 s × DT_PlayerAircraftCost.RespawnRate, and check the respawn-point picker (Respawn_A..E of the pilot's faction) and the ALivePlayerPlane.OnRespawnFinish broadcast.

Confirm with UE4SS that GI+0x878 is InformationManager_, +0x8e0 UserDataManager_, +0x910 StrixManager_, +0x928 NetworkManager_ and +0x958 MissionRoomMemberManager_, and whether each is non-null in an offline session.

With the mode type set to Deathmatch, check which damage-rate table the damage code uses (OnlinePlayerCategoryDamageRateDataTable vs PlayerCategoryDamageRateDataTable), e.g. by comparing a known missile hit on a fighter offline vs in the DM map.
Identify what GameMode+0x588 (written 8 by the SoloPVP and DM ctors) and +0x584 (ALiveGameMode ctor 1) are, by watching them during a DM boot. Candidates: max players/factions and min players.

report.summary: In AC8 Online Mode, the game that detects a hit is the one where the attacker's own plane is locally controlled. Who may damage whom is decided by one native check, CanBeDamagedBy, which reads a network-role byte at +0xED8. The role values are 1 for every offline object, 3 for your own plane online (and for AI on the room owner's game), and 2 for any remote copy. The rules are: a remote player's plane (role 2) can never cause damage; a remote copy can only be hit by the local role-3 plane; AI can never hurt a remote copy. So a missile or gun round from player A on player B is resolved only on A's PC, against A's copy of B. The opponent's replayed missiles and gun on your own screen are cosmetic. In a Strix room (StrixManager+0x1FA set), TakeDamage does not change health. It runs the plane's own pre-steps on the victim copy (the DeathToEndure and EndureInvincibleTime parts, damage-rate tables, clamping to health plus armour pool). It then sends an FLiveMessageDamage report to the victim's NetworkId over the reliable room relay. The fields are AttackerNetworkTypeId/Id, WeaponNumber, WeaponId, DamageType, an integer Damage, Attribute bits (bit 7 means the sender is the room owner), Killed and ElectronicMeasureData. FLiveMessageDamageClient is never built by the client: its class factory is its only reference. It therefore comes from Bandai's Strix server, and the room owner answers it with the full authoritative apply (clamp, set Killed when lethal, chain damage to child and parent objects) and sends back an FLiveMessageDamage result. Every game that receives an FLiveMessageDamage runs ApplyDamageResult on its own object for that NetworkId. That lowers health (armour pool first), adds to DamageHistoryMap and the last-player-attacker record, and when Killed is set calls ModifyHealthInternal(-FLT_MAX) with the attacker as causer, so the plane dies with kill credit on every PC. Each owner also sends FLiveMessageHealth (a float, every 500 ms), which copies accept only while the value is above 0 and the copy is alive, so it never kills or revives. Crash damage types 7, 8 and 9 skip the attacker checks; a lethal crash of a local plane sets Killed and is sent too. In Deathmatch the indirect-kill rule (bCalcIndirectKillScore=true in DT_GameModeScoreCalculationTable) credits the last player attacker when a player plane dies without a player causer. RVNG's current assumption that a crash is a death without a kill is therefore wrong for this game mode. Offline, which is RVNG's case, the same TakeDamage takes the local-apply branch: it applies the damage itself and then calls BroadcastDamage, which builds the same FLiveMessageDamage but drops it because there is no Strix connection. RVNG's link can capture the native result there, deliver it into ApplyDamageResult on the other PC, and replace the server and Health traffic. The local plane's role must be 3 as it is online, or CanBeDamagedBy refuses your hits on the opponent's role-2 copy.

findings.topic: CanBeDamagedBy rules (target=this, attacker=causer)
findings.finding: Body 0x15C709B60 (stub jmp at 0x147D1A990): (1) attacker is a player plane with role 2 -> false. (2) target role 2 and attacker is AI -> false. (3) target role 1 and attacker role 2 -> false. (4) target role 2 -> false if there is no attacker or the attacker is role 1, otherwise true. (5) everything else -> true. Consequences: a remote player's shots never damage anything on another PC. A remote copy can only be damaged by the local role-3 plane (or a non-AI, non-role-1 object). AI hits on a human are decided on that human's own PC. Offline the local plane is role 1, so rule 4 refuses its hits on a role-2 copy. Seen in game: Survival T1e (2026-10-30, old build) logged two AI missile hits on a role-2 copy reaching player TakeDamage and returning 0. The 0.73.20 'ghosts' finding: every hit or kill dealt with a role-2 player plane as cause was refused.

findings.topic: TakeDamage pipeline and the authority branch
findings.finding: Player TakeDamage 0x147D49D30 runs first (vtable +0xA38). It refuses damage while a component's state is 5 and during the invulnerability timer +0x3AE0. It applies the parts DeathToEndure (EPartsParameterList 833 = 0x341: a lethal hit of 25 or more leaves 1 HP) and EndureInvincibleTime (834 = 0x342: sets +0x3AE0), read through 0x147D65B40(loadout +0x1328, id). It then tail-calls game-object TakeDamage 0x147D0FDE0, which does in order: +0xDB9 gate; damage types 7/8/9 skip the attacker checks; CanBeDamagedBy; CanTakeDamage 0x147D12950 (active +0x3F4, alive, hostility via vf+0x8D8 or bCanBeDamagedByAlly +0xB50, invincible +0x3F8/+0x3F9); damage modifier vf+0xA40 (player 0x147D4A090: attacker +0x1174 multiplier when the game mode's vf+0xA10 is true, plus per-category rate arrays attacker+0x1330 / victim+0x1340); clamp to health + armour pool (vf+0x930 = pool +0x1400 x0.1) minus MinHealth. It then builds the info struct and branches at 0x147D10371: if StrixManager(GI+0x910)+0x1FA (in an online room) and not (NetworkManager(GI+0x928)+0x739 and NetworkManager.IsHost()), it only reports through BroadcastDamage 0x147D1AF10. Otherwise it calls the authoritative apply 0x147D104A0. NetworkManager+0x739 is set to 1 only by ALiveCampaignGameMode vtable 0x14CBB1E18 slot +0x398 (0x1478DB480, write at 0x1478DB60E) and cleared by the ctor (0x1474ACB47) and 0x1471C5242. Online modes therefore always take the report path; offline (RVNG) always takes the authoritative local apply.

findings.topic: Authoritative apply and ApplyDamageResult
findings.finding: AuthoritativeApply 0x147D104A0(victim, info): if alive, clamps Damage to health+pool and sets Killed when lethal; calls ApplyDamageResult; when the victim is dead, damages child objects (+0x508 list) by their MaxHealth; passes damage x DamageRateToParent (+0xCBC) to the parent (+0x518); and always ends with BroadcastDamage(victim, info). ApplyDamageResult 0x147D1B070(victim, info) does nothing on a dead victim. Otherwise it resolves the attacker's weapon (attacker vf+0x960(WeaponNumber)) and calls ApplyHealthDamage 0x147D10820. That function lowers health via ModifyHealthInternal vf+0x938 with -damage (player 0x147D4A450 drains the armour pool +0x1400 first), adds damage to DamageHistoryMap +0xE70 for the causer, and runs HUD/score/evaluation work. If Killed is set it calls vf+0x938(-3.4e38, type 1, causer=attacker), killing the plane with credit unless MinHealth>0. It also runs 0x147D0BD90 for player planes. ApplyDamageResult never sends anything, so injecting into it cannot echo.

findings.topic: Damage info struct (native, passed between the functions above)
findings.finding: +0x00 float Damage; +0x04 u8 DamageType (event+0x18); +0x08 attacker game object; +0x10 u8 WeaponNumber (projectile+0x3A8); +0x11 u8 WeaponId (projectile+0x2B1); +0x18 attacker weapon object (filled by ApplyDamageResult); +0x20 u8 Killed; +0x21 victim vf+0xB78 flag; +0x22 projectile lock-ons>1 (multi-lock); +0x23 victim vf+0xAC0 flag; +0x24 event+0x19; +0x28 TArray electronic-counter list (16-byte elements); +0x38 TArray support list. findings.topic: Send path
findings.finding: BroadcastDamage 0x147D1AF10 reads IsHost = NetworkManager.IsHost() (0x1474B38D0). IsHost returns false for ELiveGameModeType Lobby (200), true when not in a Strix room, and otherwise compares the member id with the room owner id via 0x1474EFB30/0x1474EFC20 and NM+0x520. BroadcastDamage then calls SendDamage 0x1474A9360(victim's NetworkObject +0xED0, info, IsHost) only when the victim has a network object. SendDamage builds the message (constructor 0x1474BBEC0), stamps the target id and time, and sends it with 0x1474A2190. That function reads the Strix context 0x14E4C5818 (it returns if that is null, so nothing is sent offline) and calls 0x14A4379A0(channel 0, dl=1, msg), which looks like the Strix RelayMessageWithReliable (isReliable=1).

findings.topic: Receive path and the server's role
findings.finding: Each player plane's network object registers handlers in 0x1474A7C70. Damage -> 0x1474AA990 -> ApplyNetworkDamage 0x1474AACB0(netobj, msg, false). DamageClient -> 0x1474AAAE0, which converts it to a Damage message and calls ApplyNetworkDamage(..., true). Health is a periodic queued pair (500 ms, via 0x1474A1F10). ApplyNetworkDamage resolves the attacker through the network-id map StrixManager+0x2E0 (0x1474BBFE0), runs the damage-cheat check (0x1474A3CB0, which does not block the damage), and rebuilds the info struct. With flag false (Damage) it always runs ApplyDamageResult on the target. With flag true (DamageClient), the room owner runs AuthoritativeApply 0x147D104A0, which applies the damage and re-broadcasts the result; a non-owner applies it only when Attribute bit 7 is set. Incoming messages are routed by target NetworkId (0x1474EF6B8); a Damage for an unknown id is queued in NM+0x5B8 (0x1474B8A50). The DamageClient vtable 0x14BFD70B0 is referenced only by its deserialization factory 0x1452B40D0, so the client never creates DamageClient and it must be made by Bandai's Strix server extension (jp.co.soft_gear.strix.server.ext.message.game.FLiveMessageDamageClient). ScoreUpdate and RequestRespawn are the same: factory-only, so server-made. That the server turns clients' Damage reports into DamageClient for the room owner is inferred, not seen.

findings.topic: What each PC shows for the other player's health
findings.finding: The copy's HealthInternal changes only through (a) damage results applied by ApplyDamageResult and (b) FLiveMessageHealth from the owner. The Health handler 0x1474AA800 calls SetHealth (vf+0x918) only when msg.Health>0 and the copy is alive (dead flag +0xDB8 clear, HealthInternal>0), so Health never kills and never revives a copy. It is sent from a cached message every 500 ms (queue period 0x1F4 x10000 ticks). Copies take the armour pool through ModifyHealthInternal, but nothing seen syncs the pool, so it can drift. The HUD's DMG% is GetDamagePercentage on the copy. Whether only role-3 owners send Health, and whether the value includes the pool, was not traced.

findings.topic: Remote missiles, gun and proximity fuse
findings.finding: A remote player's missile is a real projectile, launched on your PC from their role-2 copy by the remote-fire path (COOP2MP T4). It can home, collide and visibly explode on you, but its TakeDamage is refused (attacker role 2), so it is cosmetic. Its end is driven by the owner. 0x147F25E10, called from the explosive weapon's hit path 0x147F215C0 (bHit=1) and from 0x147F2249C, sends ExplosiveWeaponHit{WeaponNetworkId = projectile+0x6E8, bHit} through the game mode's network object (gm+0x738), but only when the projectile owner is role 3. Receivers find the projectile whose +0x6E8 matches and call vf+0x768 (hit) or vf+0x738. The gun works the same way: the remote trigger +0x311 replays bullets that can't damage, while the shooter's real bullets hit the copy on the shooter's PC. Proximity fuse and area damage run on the shooter's PC against the victim copy (inferred from the same rules; not traced). Flares: the victim's PushFlare is replayed on the shooter's PC, so whether flares decoy the missile is decided there.

findings.topic: Kill credit, crashes and the Deathmatch rules
findings.finding: A kill is credited to the causer passed with Killed, which is the attacker resolved from the message, through ModifyHealthInternal; DamageHistoryMap holds per-attacker totals. When a player plane dies without a player causer (a crash, or AI), ApplyHealthDamage uses the last player attacker weak pointer +0x498 as the killer and writes the kill into the killer's Evaluation (+0x16C8, via 0x147455450) with the time since match start. It does this only when GameModeScoreCalculation feature 13 (bCalcIndirectKillScore) is on for the current ELiveGameModeType (0x1471B57B0 -> InformationManager 0x147350FE0, jump table row+0x9+i). From the current paks, DT_GameModeScoreCalculationTable has Deathmatch: bCalcPlayerDamageScore, bCalcPlayerKillScore, bCalcIndirectKillScore and bCalcOverallScoreRank true, all others false. TeamDeathmatch and PvPvE also credit indirect kills. Campaign and FreeFlight do not. +0x498/+0x4A0 are set by ModifyHealthInternal and expire after a settings timeout (+0x740 per the old-build doc). Crash damage (types 7/8/9) skips CanBeDamagedBy. A lethal crash on a local plane (vf+0xC38) sets Killed and is applied locally at once; online it is also reported, so copies die with Killed. The DM event package's ObjectDestroy trigger (attacker LocalPlayer, victim EnemyPlayer, Category_Plane) drives the AWACS kill callouts, so the opponent's copy really has to die on the killer's PC.

findings.topic: Damage rates, armour pool and parts for players online
findings.finding: ULiveInformationManager keeps separate CampaignPlayerCategoryDamageRateDataMap_ (+0x578) and OnlinePlayerCategoryDamageRateDataMap_ (+0x5C8). DT_CategoryDamageRateForPlayerDataTable_ON (current paks) gives percent by AttackCategory (EPlaneCategory 0 Fighter, 1 Multirole, 2 Attacker, 3 Electronic) against Category01..11. Fighter: 110/110/110/110, 125/125, 50 x5. Multirole: 100 for all. Attacker: 85 x4, 75/75, 150 x3, 100/100. Electronic: 100 for all. The campaign table differs only in Fighter Cat07-11 (87.5) and Attacker Cat05-06 (87.5). Reading Category01-04 as player-plane categories and 05-11 as NPCs comes from the EPartsParameterList CategoryDamageRate* order, which is an inference; on that reading PvP rates are the same in both tables. The armour pool +0x13FC max / +0x1400 current (x10) is drained first and probably comes from part PA_ExHealth (65); that mapping is inferred. Other relevant parts: PA_EffectivenessOfDamage (58), PA_HealthRecovery* (60-63), DoubleLockonMissileDamage (794), DeathToEndure (833), EndureInvincibleTime (834). All of these run on the PC that executes TakeDamage, which for PvP is the shooter's PC working on the victim's copy and its loadout object +0x1328.

findings.topic: Things that do NOT apply damage (Survival findings)
findings.finding: The GameplayStatics.ApplyDamage UFUNCTION does nothing to Live objects. ModifyHealth returns 0 on a player plane because vf+0xAA0 is true. SetMinHealth keeps whole points only. Survival never destroys a live remote player plane mid-level (doing so crashed in a parallel weapon target search). Survival's co-op stand-ins and sv_coop.lua's damage relay are mod-made substitutes, not the game's model.

findings.topic: RVNG's current assumption
findings.finding: E:/ACE8 PVP/docs/GAME_INTEGRATION.md:22 and mod/ProjectRVNG/Scripts/main.lua:208-237 credit kills to the last pilot who damaged the victim, treat crashes as deaths without a kill, and hook a placeholder '/Script/TODO.AircraftPawn:ReceiveDamage'. The game has no such reflected damage event (damage is native). In Deathmatch it credits crashes to the last player attacker (bCalcIndirectKillScore).

rvngImplications: Authority model to reproduce: the PC whose own plane fired the weapon detects the hit, and an authority applies it and sends the result (online the room owner, with Bandai's server routing reports to it). RVNG has no server, so make each PC the authority for the hits its own weapons make: offline TakeDamage already runs the authoritative local apply (0x147D104A0) on the victim copy. Make each PC the authority for its own plane's crashes and environment damage too. This matches what the game does for the room owner's own hits, with no extra round trip.

Roles: keep the opponent's copy at role 2 (the remote spawn sets it). After the local spawn, set your own plane's +0xED8 to 3, as the game does online (0x1471B697C). At offline role 1, CanBeDamagedBy refuses your hits on the role-2 copy. Do not set StrixManager+0x1FA to fake 'online': it switches TakeDamage to report-only and other code would make Strix calls.

Capture: hook BroadcastDamage 0x147D1AF10(victim, info) (2026-11-02 build; unique 24-byte prologue in findings). It runs after every authoritative apply, for your own plane and for the opponent's copy, before the network-object check. Serialize exactly the FLiveMessageDamage fields: target id, attacker id, WeaponNumber, WeaponId, DamageType (after the 0x68->0x1B / 0x69->0x1A remap), integer Damage, Attribute bits, Killed. SendDamage itself never runs for a plane with no network object and drops the message offline.

Apply on the other PC: map the target id to that PC's object (the own plane for hits on the copy, the copy for the sender's own-plane results). Build the info struct as ApplyNetworkDamage does (Damage=float(int), +0x4 type, +0x8 attacker, +0x10/+0x11 weapon, +0x20 Killed, +0x21..+0x24 bits, arrays empty) and call ApplyDamageResult 0x147D1B070. Or call ApplyNetworkDamage 0x1474AACB0(netobj, msg, false), but only if the attacker is registered in StrixManager+0x2E0, or kill credit is lost. Never inject through the DamageClient path: it re-runs the authoritative apply, re-broadcasts, and would loop through your hook.

Health: send your own plane's GetHealth about every 500 ms (FLiveMessageHealth semantics) and apply it on the copy only when it is above 0 and the copy is alive (calling the native handler 0x1474AA800 or SetHealth vf+0x918 is equivalent). Do not send the opponent copy's health. The copy's health is what the shooter's PC uses for the clamp and the Killed verdict, so keep it fresh.

Missiles and gun: keep the replayed weapons cosmetic. The game already refuses their damage, so never deal damage from them. Forward an ExplosiveWeaponHit equivalent (projectile +0x6E8 id, bHit) from the owner so replayed missiles end when the owner's did. Forward flares (PushFlare) promptly, because flare evasion is decided on the shooter's PC.

Kill credit and stats: let the native Killed / ModifyHealthInternal(-FLT_MAX, attacker) path kill the plane on both PCs. Then DamageHistoryMap, +0x498, Evaluation and ObjectDestroy triggers (attacker LocalPlayer on the killer's PC) all fire natively, and RVNG can read kills there rather than inferring them. For crashes, forward the victim's Killed=1 crash result: the copy then dies on the opponent's PC, where +0x498 still names the shooter, so the indirect kill is credited the game's way. That needs the mission's ELiveGameModeType to be Deathmatch (3), because Campaign and FreeFlight rows have bCalcIndirectKillScore false. Update RVNG's rule 'crashes are deaths without a kill' to the game's: an indirect kill goes to the last player attacker within the window.

Hostility: CanTakeDamage 0x147D12950 refuses ally hits unless bCanBeDamagedByAlly (+0xB50) is set or the damage is a crash. The opponent's copy and your own plane must therefore be enemies (faction or game-mode relation vf+0x8D8), as in Deathmatch ('EnemyPlayer').

Parts and rates run on the PC that runs TakeDamage, which is the shooter's PC acting on the victim's copy. The copy must carry the victim's real loadout object (+0x1328, parts such as DeathToEndure and EndureInvincibleTime) and plane id, as the native remote spawn sets them up. The online player damage-rate table is only guaranteed if the offline build uses OnlinePlayerCategoryDamageRateDataMap_.

Avoid desync loops: never forward results produced by applying a received message (ApplyDamageResult does not broadcast, so injecting there is safe). Filter the BroadcastDamage hook so that results for the copy are sent only when they came from your own TakeDamage. Do not destroy the remote plane on death; let the native death and respawn flow run.
blockers: No Strix server: FLiveMessageDamageClient, ScoreUpdate and RequestRespawn are only ever created by the server (client factories only). The room-owner authority loop (report -> DamageClient -> authoritative apply -> result) cannot run as-is offline, so RVNG must take the server's place or use the shooter-authoritative local-apply branch.
Offline the local plane is role 1, and CanBeDamagedBy refuses role-1 attackers against role-2 copies. RVNG must set its own plane to role 3, which is untested offline.
The send function 0x1474A2190 returns when the Strix context 0x14E4C5818 is null, so no native message leaves the PC. RVNG must capture at BroadcastDamage, not at the network layer.
Attacker resolution in ApplyNetworkDamage uses StrixManager+0x2E0, which the COOP2MP work found empty offline. Without registering ids, use ApplyDamageResult with an explicit attacker pointer.

Indirect-kill credit and other score features depend on the mission row's ELiveGameModeType (InformationManager mission table row +0x6C). An offline mission typed Campaign or FreeFlight disables them.

The exact server routing (which members get DamageClient, whether the room relay echoes to the sender, what fills Damage.Health +0x34) cannot be seen in the client and cannot be tested by modded clients without EasyAntiCheat.
openQuestions: Solo test: set your own plane's +0xED8=3 offline, spawn a role-2 copy (Survival's SV_CoopSpawnPP style) hostile to you, and fire a missile at it. Expected log: CanBeDamagedBy true, AuthoritativeApply runs, the copy's HealthInternal drops, and BroadcastDamage is called with the right Damage, WeaponNumber and Killed. Also check whether role 3 offline breaks anything (HUD, lock-on, PlaneWeaponsFired, ExplosiveWeaponHit send).

Does the role-2 copy take terrain or sea collision damage (types 7/8/9) on the remote PC when its RemoteUpdate flies it into the ground? Fly a fed copy into terrain and log TakeDamage(type, causer) on it and its health.
Offline, does the local player plane have a ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane (+0xED0), and is anything registered in StrixManager+0x2E0? Read both after spawn.

Inject an ApplyDamageResult with Killed=1 and the copy as causer on your own plane, in a mission whose mode type is Deathmatch. Do the kill camera, DM respawn flow, DamageHistoryMap entry and the ObjectDestroy (EnemyPlayer) trigger all fire, and is the evaluation kill recorded for the copy?

Crash credit: damage the copy, then crash it by forwarding a Killed=1 type-7 result. On the shooter's PC, does ApplyHealthDamage credit the last player attacker (+0x498) within the window? Read the window length (the settings +0x740 field in this build).

Which damage-rate table offline: log the plane's +0x1330 and +0x1340 float arrays on spawn to see whether the Online or Campaign category table is used. They differ only for NPC categories and the Attacker-vs-Cat05-06 rate.
What does the owner put in FLiveMessageHealth: GetHealth only, or including the armour pool? Find the writer of the cached message (netobj+0xF8) and compare with +0x1400.
Online-only (cannot be tested modded): does Strix's room relay echo a sender's message back to it, and does the server turn non-owner Damage reports into DamageClient for the room owner only?

Player TakeDamage (0x147D49D30) multiplies the damage by the victim's loadout float loadout(+0x1328)+0x1A7FC (skipped for DamageType 0xE). ApplyNetworkDamage's cheat check 0x1474A3CB0 compares msg WeaponId with attacker vf+0x960(WeaponNumber)+0x2B1 when DamageType == 0xD. ApplyNetworkDamage always rebuilds the info with empty electronic and support arrays, so ElectronicMeasureData is not reapplied on receivers.

GO TakeDamage has native 'can't finish' rules: if victim +0x3BD is set and the attacker is AI (vf+0xAB0), the damage is clamped to leave 1 HP (0x147D0FF99-0x147D0FFC7). AuthoritativeApply itself ignores MinHealth and sets Killed whenever damage >= health+pool.

NM+0x739 = 1 is written unconditionally by campaign mode slot +0x398 (0x1478DB480; vtable 0x14CBB1E18, whose campaign slots moved -0x28 in this build: finish reason at +0xAC0, CreateEndSequence at +0xAD0). Any online session run under a campaign-derived mode would therefore be room-owner-authoritative. Deathmatch is not, so in DM even the owner reports and waits for a server DamageClient.

The info struct's +0x22 is projectile+0x3C8 > 1 and +0x10/+0x11 are projectile +0x3A8/+0x2B1. These are the same projectile bytes PlaneWeaponsFired's sender reads (COOP2MP.md). report.summary: The game runs a deathmatch through a native state machine with no reflected match functions. The deathmatch mode BP (BP_ChronicleDeathMatchGameMode) holds only data. The logic lives in the C++ chain ALiveGameMode > ALiveOnlineGameMode > ALiveSoloPVPGameMode > ALiveDeathMatchGameMode. The online mode keeps the ELiveOnlineGameModeState byte at ALiveOnlineGameMode+0x758 and calls one virtual Enter and one virtual Tick function per state. Every client runs its own copy of the machine. It sends its state to the room through ULiveNetworkManager (GameInstance.NetworkManager_), and the Sync states wait until all room members reach the same state. The room owner (StrixManager_+0x1fa) sets the match clock (FLiveMessageGameTime with BeginningTime, FinishTime and bSetByHost). Leaving SyncStartMatch also waits on a Strix room property named "phaseIndex". The match starts on Enter GamePlaying, which seeds ScoreRankList and calls the start hook (+0xb28). The deathmatch's GamePlaying tick sums each player's native score map (ALiveGameObject+0xe08) and compares it to VictoryScore in the mission config (500000). It also fires the RankChanged EP trigger when the local rank changes. A deathmatch is decided on score, not kill count: the score is player kill plus damage plus indirect-kill score (DT_GameModeScoreCalculationTable). Every finish goes through OnGameFinish (+0xab8). The reason is stored at mode+0x538 (1 Special, 2 Timeup, 3 VictoryScore, 4 ForcedTermination). OnGameFinish creates a ULiveOnlineMissionEndSequence and sends a PreparingMissionEnd message. The deathmatch override then fires the DM_MissionFinish EP trigger with (reason, local rank). The machine then runs GameTerminating, the ending IGC and SyncEvaluation (all members exchange evaluations), then Ended, which travels to /Game/OnlineMode/Maps/Menu/Result. When a player leaves, the game uses the same PreparingMissionEnd path: RecvPreparingMissionEnd (+0xdd0) sets ForcedTermination and marks the result Aborted (no result) or Finished (counted). The deathmatch row of DT_MissionContents gives ConnectionsLeftNum=1, MissionSuccessSeconds=105, BaseRespawnTime=10 and AllowBot=false. On respawn, the plane's +0xbf0 function picks a respawn point, sends the respawn to the network, moves the plane (+0xbf8), runs OnRestored, fires the RespawnedPlayer EP trigger and broadcasts OnRespawnFinish. The other clients replay it on their copy of the plane with RespawnAtPoint. Scores are kept in sync the same way: the client that works out a hit or kill sends FLiveMessageScoreAddition, and the receivers call AddScore (+0xc10) on that plane. For RVNG this means the native ranking, victory, HUD, radio and finish logic can be reused unchanged, but only if RVNG's P2P link fills the gaps Strix fills: member states, the shared clock, the phaseIndex start gate, score and respawn mirroring, and PreparingMissionEnd. None of these points is a reflected UFUNCTION, so detecting and driving them needs native code (Survival-style runtime plus signatures). Lua can only observe some side effects: reflected arrays and config, HUD text, EP triggers, the OnRestored event and the end-sequence object.

findings.topic: Room to loading to start
findings.finding: WaitingNetworkInitialize Tick (+0xc68, 0x1471c6230) sets up the Strix channel 'default' through NetworkManager_ and MissionRoomMemberManager_ (+0x958) and then advances at once; it does not wait. LoadPlayerPlane Tick (+0xc88) advances once byte +0x5f1 is set. TimeSync Enter (+0xca0) sets LoadingPercentageManager+0x50 to 0.5. TimeSync Tick (+0xca8, 0x1471c6810) waits until the number of members at state 5 or later (0x1474cc700 on NetworkManager+0x210) reaches the member count. The host then sends the game times through 0x1474b6a60 with mode +0x4a8, +0x4b0 and +0x4b8; a client instead waits until some member reaches state 6. Both then call vfunc +0xa30 (SoloPVP: faction assignment) and advance. SyncStartMatch Enter (+0xd18) makes the host stamp sync time and set NPC_RANDOM_LOTTERY_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 30) and calls GameMode.NetworkObject (+0x738) 0x1474a61f0. SyncStartMatch Tick (+0xd20) advances only when 0x1471c1050 is true. That function reads the Strix member property 'phaseIndex' (UTF-16 at 0x14cb3d520) through 0x1474ed840 and returns value >= 1; Online tutorials skip the check. Non-hosts also register a 'SyncStartMatchTick' timer. CallStartMatch Enter (+0xd28) jumps to +0xc10, which fills ScoreRankList from the world manager. CallStartMatch Tick (0x1471afa90) calls vfunc +0x938 and advances. Enter GamePlaying (+0xd38, 0x1471c7c70) calls +0xb28, the start hook (the deathmatch's version plays local cue id 6). The start therefore depends on Strix room data and the host's clock; nothing in the client starts the match by itself.

findings.topic: Match clock and time-up
findings.finding: The remaining-time function (+0xa88, 0x1471b9a60) returns (mode+0x4b8 FinishTime minus now) scaled to seconds. 'Now' is the pause time at +0x4c0 when it is set, otherwise the synchronized clock (0x147907550/0x147907660). Setters +0xa68, +0xa70 and +0xa78 write +0x4a8, +0x4b0 and +0x4b8 (Online slots 333-335), so the clock is an absolute time sent by the host. The GamePlaying pre-tick (0x1471bca40) refreshes the local HUD timer (HUD+0x550) and calls +0xb98 (0x1471c9bb0), which fires the time EP triggers (0x20-0x22, including RemainingTime). Time-up is +0xb38 (0x1471c93c0): it calls the base, sets mode+0x538=2 (Timeup) and calls +0xab8. 0x1471c93xx sends the time-up (counter +0x584) through NetworkManager.NetworkObject 0x1474ce590 when this client is the room owner. Messages involved: FLiveMessageTimeUp, FLiveMessageGameTime, FLiveMessageRealTime and FLiveMessagePauseTime. It is not settled whether the 210 s MissionLimitTime or a server value sets FinishTime: EP_DM's RemainingTime_60 line is 'passed_4min', which implies a 300 s match.

findings.topic: Spawn points, factions and initial placement
findings.finding: SoloPVP +0xa30 (0x1471e0230) runs once TimeSync finishes. It builds the names ALPHA..ZULU, takes the world manager's player list (0x147208fc0(world)+0x138/+0x140), sorts it (0x1473b6430), and gives each player plane its own ELiveFaction (Alpha+i) at ALiveGameObject.Faction (+0x3b2), helped by 0x1474b6700 on plane+0x2200. TeleportPlayers Tick (+0xcd8, 0x1471c6c90) and respawns use the spawn-point picker 0x147391240(world manager, selector, plane) and the point location 0x147d188e0. Spawn points are ALivePlayerStart and FLivePlayerStartDesc (Faction, PointAssinment ELivePlayerStartAssinment {Start, Respawn_A..E}, bCanChaoice). The local player plane is world manager+0x1e0.

findings.topic: Respawn (native chain)
findings.finding: ALivePlayerPlane vtable is 0x14cbef168. +0xbf0 = 0x147d5ccd0, Respawn(uint8 selector, bool skipMove): it picks a point (0x147391240), calls RespawnAtPoint 0x147d18c80(plane, pointId, skipMove), then 0x147d187f0. If vfunc +0xc38 is true it broadcasts OnRespawnFinish (+0x3c18), then clears +0x3c28/+0x3c2c. RespawnAtPoint resolves the point and, if NetworkObject (+0xed0) exists, sends the respawn through 0x1474a98e0 before calling +0xbf8. +0xbf8 = 0x147D5CD60, RespawnAt(loc, rot, skipMove). It teleports (+0x5d0), runs SetActive, ProcessEvent(OnRestored) and an OnRestoredDelegate (+0x350) broadcast, clears the input blocks +0x13b8..+0x13be, and fires EP trigger 0x62 RespawnedPlayer (0x147d5d07e). It does not touch health or invincibility. The receive side 0x1474ab402 calls RespawnAtPoint(remote plane, msg+0x20 pointId, msg+0x24 bool). Messages: FLiveMessageRequestRespawn (PlayerStartNetworkId), FLiveMessageRespawn (RespawnCancel), FLiveMessageTeleportToRespawnPoint, FLiveMessageRequestTeleportToRespawnPoint, FLiveMessageRespawnTimeEnd and FLiveMessageDestroyedLocation. Survival has run +0xbf8 in game on this build ('respawn: the player plane's respawn 147D5CD60 (vtable +bf8)' ... 'respawned at ...', 2026-11-17).

findings.topic: Death, death camera and respawn trigger
findings.finding: The death camera and respawn screen use these pieces: ULiveKillCameraOnlineWidget (LiveHUD.KillCameraOnlineWidgetClass), ELiveHUDMode KillCamera and Respawn, ALiveIGCRespawn (BP_IGCRespawn plus igc_respawn_wait_cam), LiveImpactCameraParameter.RespawnCamera*, and the pause screen ELiveNUIInGamePauseMode::Respawn with ULiveNUIInGamePauseRespawnWidget (AutomaticRespawnTime gauge) and RespawnPointWidgets ('Online_Hud_RespawnPoint_A..E_Name'). The point-select code 0x1475d4b70 maps 'Start' and 'A'..'D' and calls local plane +0xbf0. The only other caller of +0xbf0 found is the takeoff/landing component (ELiveTakeoffAndLandingState RespawnWait) at 0x147d6e6e3. Respawn delay comes from ALiveGameMode.BaseRespawnTime (+0x3d0, constructor default 10.0f at 0x1471b4641; deathmatch row 10), parts parameters RespawnTime/MP_ReducesRespawn, and the RESPAWN_TIME_SUBTRACT_RATE config key. What opens the respawn screen after a deathmatch death, and whether a timer auto-respawns, was not traced. No respawn invulnerability was found in the respawn functions.

findings.topic: Scoring: who counts, where it lives
findings.finding: Each ALiveGameObject has a non-reflected score map at +0xe08 (score-type byte to value). 0x147d19600(obj) returns the total as a float and 0x147d19800(obj, type) returns one type. The game-object vfuncs +0xc10 AddScore(TArray<{u8 type,int value}>) (base 0x147d191f0) and +0xc18 SetScore (base 0x147d19390) change it; the player plane overrides them (0x147d5db20 / 0x147d5dc00) to update the HUD score popup (0x147d5e220) and LiveEvaluation (+0x16c8). Locally, the death/damage processing at 0x147d11055 walks the per-attacker score list. For each attacker it sends the scores through that attacker's NetworkObject (0x1474a9c70, FLiveMessageScoreAddition) and then calls attacker->AddScore. The receive handlers are 0x1474abbce (calls +0xc10, ScoreAddition) and 0x1474abd7d (calls +0xc18, ScoreUpdate); the entries are FLiveMessageScoreData {ScoreType, value}. The client that resolves a hit or kill scores it and sends it to the others. ScoreRankList (ALiveGameMode+0x718, reflected) is filled at CallStartMatch (+0xc10, 0x1471c0100) and sorted by +0xc18 (0x1471d84c0). +0xc20 returns the top player if its score is above 0; +0xc28 returns a pawn's index in the ranking.

findings.topic: Deathmatch GamePlaying tick: victory score and rank changes
findings.finding: The deathmatch's +0xd40 (0x1471df440) first runs the online GamePlaying tick (0x1471c7e80: defeat stages, threat level). It then runs 0x1471df5f0, unless vfunc +0xb80 says the match is already finished. That function reads VictoryScore (mission config +0x200) and, for each plane in world manager+0x138, ends the match with mode+0x538=3 (VictoryScore) and a call to +0xab8 as soon as 0x147d19600(plane) >= VictoryScore. Next it gets the local rank (+0xc28 on world manager+0x1e0). If the rank differs from the previous one (DM +0x828, initially -1), it fires EP trigger 0x17 RankChanged with TargetPlayer, Top (rank==0) and RankDown (old<=new) through 0x14720f490. The deathmatch's +0xc40 (0x1471df740) calls the online ranking update and builds a faction-to-score map from Faction (+0x3b2) and score. RankingForPlayers (DM +0x830) is reflected.
sources: online_gm2.txt 0x1471df440-0x1471df5b5 (mov byte ptr [rax],0x17 at 0x1471df4f2), 0x1471df5f0-0x1471df73b (mov byte ptr [rsi+0x538],3 at 0x1471df71f)

findings.topic: End of match: OnGameFinish and the end sequence
findings.finding: ALiveOnlineGameMode::OnGameFinish (+0xab8, 0x1471c9580; string 'ALiveOnlineGameMode::OnGameFinish') runs once, guarded by mode+0x521. It calls +0xac8 (0x1471c9800), which creates a ULiveOnlineMissionEndSequence (StaticClass 0x146ee7ef0) in MissionEndSequence (+0x3d8). It then calls +0xac0 and 0x1471b9c90(1,1), notifies NetworkManager_ (0x1474b5a30). When this client is the room owner it sends the end through NetworkManager.NetworkObject (0x1474ce080) and GameMode.NetworkObject 0x1474a64d0(mode+0x729, +0x72a, remaining time) (FLiveMessageMissionEnd). Outside Online tutorials and free flight it then calls 0x1471cb5e0, which sends PreparingMissionEnd and sets PREPARING_MISSION_END_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 30). Every finish reason is at mode+0x538 (ELiveFinishConditionType): +0xab0 sets 1 (Special, used by the EP finish node), +0xb38 sets 2 (Timeup), the deathmatch victory check sets 3 (VictoryScore) and RecvPreparingMissionEnd sets 4 (ForcedTermination). +0xdc8 returns 2 when the reason is Timeup, else 1. The deathmatch's +0xab8 (0x1471df1f0) calls the online finish, plays local cue 9 and then 0x1b, 0x1c or 0x1d (1st, other, no rank), and fires EP trigger 9 DM_MissionFinish with (mode+0x538 reason, 1-based local rank, 0 = no rank) through 0x14720f160.

findings.topic: Forced termination, leaving, host
findings.finding: ALiveOnlineGameMode::RecvPreparingMissionEnd (+0xdd0, 0x1471cb7e0; string 'ALiveOnlineGameMode::RecvPreparingMissionEnd') is called from the message receiver 0x1474c8e94 with (msg+0x14 member id, msg+0x20 bool, msg+0x21 bool). It runs the PreparingMissionEnd sync (0x1471cb5e0: stage +0x80c=1, timeout). If the match has not already ended and the message names the local member, it sets ForcedTerminationState at +0x804 to 2 (Finished) when either bool is set, else 1 (Aborted). It also sets +0x808, shows a local notice (0x147243560), sets mode+0x538=4 and calls +0xab8. GameTerminating Tick (0x1471c8190, 'ALiveOnlineGameMode::MissionEndSyncTick') waits on the +0x80c stages and +0x804. When the state is Aborted, IGCEnding Tick (0x1471c8750) skips the ending, and Ended Enter (0x1471c8f30) takes the abort path 0x1471c5f70 instead of the result travel. ELiveForcedTerminationState is {None, Aborted, Finished}. The deathmatch row's ConnectionsLeftNum (1) and MissionSuccessSeconds (105) are the forced-end rule; their reader and the side that decides to send PreparingMissionEnd when someone leaves were not found. Host role: StrixManager_+0x1fa (written as IsRoomOwner in the inference). The exe has the Strix strings StrixRoomOwnerChanged, IsRoomOwner, SendRpcToRoomOwner, LeaveRoom, 'HOSTMIGRATION' and 'client error : Disconnected from the room server'. ELiveForceDisconnectType is {None, LoadTimeout, TravelResult, Sleep, KickRoomMember, DebugError}. The deathmatch row has AllowBot=false (FLiveMessageChangeBot/OperateBot and ELiveAIBotSpawnReason::DisconnectPlayer serve other modes).
sources: online_gm2.txt 0x1471cb5e0-0x1471cba87 (mov byte ptr [rdi+0x538],4 at 0x1471cba7a; mov [r14],ecx to +0x804 at 0x1471cb93f)
exe string scan (scratch run): StrixRoomOwnerChanged 0x14bfbe7d0, HOSTMIGRATION 0x14bfa27b8, ELiveForceDisconnectType::*

findings.topic: Evaluation and results
findings.finding: SyncEvaluation Tick (0x1471c8e10) waits until every member reaches state 18. It then gathers evaluation data (LiveEvaluation 0x147455730) and advances. Ended Enter (0x1471c8f30) calls +0xb18 (0x1471c5d20) unless the match was Aborted. +0xb18 stops the deathmatch BGM ('AKE_Bgm_Online_AllMVP_Stop') and travels to ResultMapReference (+0x380, '/Game/OnlineMode/Maps/Menu/Result') through 0x147901bf0. The result map has BP_ResultAvatarGameMode and WBP_Menu_Result_000, and ULiveNUIMenuResultPreviewBaseWidget has parts named *_DM01 (MVP and PlayerList). The data path is ULiveNetworkResultManager (GameInstance.NetworkResultManager_, TMap<FString, ULiveNetworkResultObject*> NetworkResultObject) plus FLiveMessageResultState (ResultState, EvaluationUsersList), FLiveMessageEvaluationList/EvaluationData/EvaluationAccumulateData, FLiveMessageResultEmote and FLiveMessageMissionClear (MatchResult ELiveMatchResultType {None, Win, Lose, Draw}). The FLiveMissionResult* structs and ULiveNUIMenuResultContext have no reflected fields, so Lua cannot read results except as UI text. Rewards come from Chronicle (FLiveMessageEntityUpdate*) and RESULT_START_SYNC_TIMEOUT_SEC applies.

findings.topic: Deathmatch HUD widgets
findings.finding: ULiveForEachGameModeWidget.DeathMatchInfoClass chooses ULiveDeathMatchInfoWidget (WBP_HUD_SubWidgets_Parts_DeathMatchInfo_000) with DeathMatchExInfo_000 (ULiveDeathMatchExInfoWidget). Its TextBlocks are FirstRank, FirstRankPlayerName, FirstRankScore, FirstRankCallSign, LocalRank, LocalPlayerName, LocalPlayerScore and LocalPlayerCallSign, plus color ids MainColorId and EnemyColorId. Neither widget has UFUNCTIONs; native code fills them from ScoreRankList, the score map and the Faction callsign. Lua can read the shown values with TextBlock:GetText():ToString().

findings.topic: Stock EP_DM (radio only)
findings.finding: EP_DM has 28 triggers and 22 execs, all radio or radio-queue nodes plus one SetActiveTrigger. Nothing in it ends the match or keeps score. Triggers: MissionStart (01), radio p1_dm001_start. PlayerDestroyByRank_Top (3b; LocalPlayer, EnemyPlayer, rank 1), radio shoot_enemytop, which also clears the AWACS queue. RankChanged_Top/Up/Down (17; RankUp or RankDown, Top bool). RemainingTime_60 (22), radio passed_4min. DM_MissionFinish_1st..8th and _NoRank (09; Timeup, rank 1..8 or 0), radio end_rank_top_02, with Composite (2f) groups 2-3, 4-6 and 7-8/none. ObjectDestroy_ao (70; attacker LocalPlayer, any, Category_Plane; victim EnemyPlayer, Category_Plane). EventNotifyCount_1..8 (35; counting ObjectDestroy_ao), AWACS lines pbyp_AWACS_destroy_player_v1/v2_ao_N; the 8th enables ObjectDestroy_ao_over8, which repeats. The native code fires the payloads: DM_MissionFinish (type 9 at 0x1471df38a), RankChanged (0x17) and RespawnedPlayer (0x62). The DM_MissionFinish triggers filter on Timeup, so (inferred) a VictoryScore or forced finish plays no end radio.
sources: ELiveEventTriggerType.h (index = line-7: DM_MissionFinish 9, RankChanged 0x17, RemainingTime 0x22, CompositeEvent 0x2f, EventNotifyCount 0x35, PlayerDestroyByRank 0x3b, RespawnedPlayer 0x62)

findings.topic: What Lua can observe or drive
findings.finding: No match-start, kill, leave or end UFUNCTION exists to RegisterHook. RVNG's HOOKS paths '/Script/TODO.MultiplayerGameMode:*' have no real counterpart. Reflected and reachable from Lua: GameMode.MissionConfig (VictoryScore, MissionLimitTime; writable before start), BaseRespawnTime (+0x3d0), ScoreRankList, RankingForPlayers, MissionEndSequence, NetworkObject; LivePlayerPlane.OnRespawnFinish; LiveGameObject.Faction and IsAlive; GameInstance.NetworkManager_, StrixManager_ and NetworkResultManager_ (the objects only). OnRestored, OnReposition and OnDeath are BlueprintNativeEvents; OnRestored is called through ProcessEvent in RespawnAt, so a RegisterHook on it should fire on respawn (not tested). Lua techniques Survival uses in game (NotifyOnNewObject, custom EP triggers writing LiveSetFlagInt, HUD TextBlock reads) carry over: NotifyOnNewObject('/Script/Live.LiveOnlineMissionEndSequence') marks the end, and a custom EP with ObjectDestroy LocalPlayer->EnemyPlayer, RespawnedPlayer and DM_MissionFinish can feed Lua flags. The state byte, finish reason, score map and ForcedTerminationState are not reflected and need native reads or hooks.
sources: mod/UE4SS/AC8SurvivalMode/Scripts/sv_allies.lua:598 (NotifyOnNewObject in use), docs/re/KILLS_HEALTH_DEATH.md 'How Survival should do it'

rvngImplications: Delete the placeholder hooks ('/Script/TODO.MultiplayerGameMode:OnMatchStarted/OnPlayerLeft/OnMatchEnded'). The real points are native vfuncs on ALiveOnlineGameMode, so RVNG needs a native runtime like Survival's (signatures, not addresses, because the 2026-11-02 patch moved code). Detour SetState (0x1471c6020) to see every state change, OnGameFinish (+0xab8; the deathmatch's 0x1471df1f0) to get the finish reason at mode+0x538, and RecvPreparingMissionEnd (+0xdd0, 0x1471cb7e0) to see forced ends. Lua can watch NotifyOnNewObject('/Script/Live.LiveOnlineMissionEndSequence') and the reflected GameMode.ScoreRankList and RankingForPlayers.

Run the stock deathmatch game mode (a PL_DM_00x map, MissionID 160010..160060, BP_ChronicleDeathMatchGameMode, MC_DM) rather than writing new match rules, and replace only the Strix layer it waits on. Concretely, each peer must see: (1) the other member's ELiveOnlineGameModeState in ULiveNetworkManager's member-state table (+0x210), with the member count at +0x538, so the sync states (TimeSync, SyncEvaluation, member counts) pass; (2) one peer acting as room owner (StrixManager_+0x1fa) that sends BeginningTime and FinishTime, which the other applies through setters +0xa68/+0xa70/+0xa78 on the same synchronized clock; (3) the 'phaseIndex' room property at 1 or more so SyncStartMatch advances. Alternatively, detour the Sync ticks (TimeSync Tick +0xca8, SyncStartMatch +0xd20, SyncEvaluation +0xd88) to ask RVNG's link instead.

Copy the game's own replication of scores and respawns over RVNG's link. Each peer lets its native damage/kill code score its own hits; the AddScore list (score type byte + value) is the FLiveMessageScoreAddition payload. On the receiver, call the opponent copy's AddScore (+0xc10) or SetScore (+0xc18), as the stock handlers 0x1474abbce/0x1474abd7d do. The deathmatch VictoryScore check, ranking, HUD (DeathMatchExInfo), RankChanged, PlayerDestroyByRank and DM_MissionFinish triggers then work without changes.

The deathmatch win condition is SCORE (VictoryScore 500000, damage + kill + indirect-kill points), not a kill count. RVNG's 'kill_target' rule must either become a VictoryScore value written to GameMode.MissionConfig.VictoryScore (reflected) before GamePlaying, or stay an RVNG-side counter that ends the match through the stock finish path (set mode+0x538 and call +0xab8, or use +0xab0, which sets Special(1)). Map endReason from mode+0x538: 2=time_limit, 3=score/kill target, 4=disconnect, 1=special.

Respawn the stock way. When the local pilot respawns, call ALivePlayerPlane +0xbf0 Respawn(selector, false), which picks the point, fires OnRestored, RespawnedPlayer and OnRespawnFinish, and would also send through the plane's NetworkObject. Send the chosen point (or the location and rotation) to the peer, which calls RespawnAtPoint (0x147d18c80) or +0xbf8 on its copy of the opponent, as the stock receiver 0x1474ab402 does. Reset health separately (the respawn functions don't touch it). Use BaseRespawnTime (+0x3d0, deathmatch 10 s) for the delay.

Make the opponent's ALivePlayerPlane appear in the world manager's player list (0x147208fc0(world)+0x138) before TimeSync ends. SoloPVP's faction assignment (+0xa30), the VictoryScore scan, the ranking and the EnemyPlayer trigger filters all read that list. Each pilot must end up with a different ELiveFaction (Alpha/Bravo).

Map link loss and surrender to the stock forced-termination path: call RecvPreparingMissionEnd(+0xdd0) natively with the local member id and the 'finished' flag set when more than MissionSuccessSeconds (105 s) of play has passed. The game then ends with ForcedTermination(4) and either skips results (Aborted) or keeps them (Finished), as ConnectionsLeftNum=1 intends for a deathmatch. Log it as 'disconnect'.

Expect the result screen to need data RVNG cannot supply offline (Chronicle rewards, ULiveNetworkResultManager or evaluation sync). Plan to finish at Ended, either with a forced Aborted state (path 0x1471c5f70) or by skipping the +0xb18 travel, and show RVNG's own summary from the scores RVNG mirrored.
blockers: Big blocker: the start and sync gates are tied to Strix room state: member-state counts in ULiveNetworkManager+0x210, StrixManager_+0x1fa (assumed to mean 'room owner'), and the 'phaseIndex' room property read by 0x1471c1050. An offline client with no Strix room will stall in TimeSync, SyncStartMatch or SyncEvaluation (inferred) until RVNG fakes these or detours the sync ticks.

The FLiveMessage* classes are registered by name in the function at 0x145295560. The mapping from message class to receive handler, and the exact wire field layout, were only partly traced: handlers found are ScoreAddition, ScoreUpdate, Respawn and PreparingMissionEnd. Field names come from the string pool near each message name, so which field belongs to which message is approximate.
What sends PreparingMissionEnd when a member leaves (the room owner checking ConnectionsLeftNum, or the Strix server extension 'jp.co.soft_gear.strix.server.ext.message.game') was not found.
The current UE4SS 3.0.1 Lua cannot read the native fields that matter (state +0x758, reason +0x538, score map +0xe08, +0x804), so RVNG needs a native DLL like Survival's runtime.
openQuestions: Load PL_DM_001 offline (MissionID 160010, BP_ChronicleDeathMatchGameMode) and log ALiveOnlineGameMode+0x758 and +0x57c every second through a native read: which state does it stall in without Strix?

At Enter GamePlaying (+0xd38), log +0xa88 remaining time and +0x4a8/+0x4b8. Does the clock come from MC_DM.MissionLimitTime (210 s) or from the server or room (EP_DM's 60-seconds-left line says 'passed_4min', which implies 300 s)?

Spawn the opponent as a role-2 ALivePlayerPlane (Survival SV_CoopSpawnPP) before TimeSync. Does it show up in world manager+0x138 and get Faction Bravo from SoloPVP +0xa30, and does the HUD DeathMatchExInfo list it?

Die in an offline deathmatch with a detour on ALivePlayerPlane +0xbf0 that logs its return address: does the Online mode respawn on its own after BaseRespawnTime, or only through the pause respawn UI (0x1475d4b70)?

Call the opponent copy's AddScore (+0xc10) with {type, value} entries from the link. Does the deathmatch tick end with mode+0x538=3 at VictoryScore, and do RankChanged and DM_MissionFinish fire in EP_DM (radio heard)?
Does a Lua RegisterHook('/Script/Live.LiveGameObject:OnRestored') fire when +0xbf8 runs, and does NotifyOnNewObject('/Script/Live.LiveOnlineMissionEndSequence') fire at OnGameFinish?

Hook 0x1471cb5e0 and RecvPreparingMissionEnd in a real online deathmatch (on a clean, non-modded account only, if ever allowed): who sends PreparingMissionEnd when a player leaves, and what msg+0x14/+0x20/+0x21 hold?
Read bIsInvincible and MinHealth on the plane for 5 s after a stock respawn: is there respawn invulnerability, and does the EndureInvincibleTime parts parameter apply?

After Ended in an offline run, does the +0xb18 travel to /Game/OnlineMode/Maps/Menu/Result load and fill anything, or hang waiting for result data? Compare with forcing ForcedTerminationState=Aborted (+0x804=1).

checks.correction: Writing GameMode.MissionConfig.VictoryScore is not what the DM victory check reads. It reads WorldSettings.MissionSettings.MissionConfig (or the CDO), so RVNG must write that object or first check that it is the same instance. That OnRestored is the FName ProcessEvent'd in +0xbf8 is not proven.

checks.claim: Summary and blocker: 'The room owner (StrixManager_+0x1fa) sets the match clock' and 'An offline client with no Strix room will stall in TimeSync, SyncStartMatch or SyncEvaluation'.
checks.evidence: +0x1fa is the online flag (see the state-machine check). With +0x1fa==0: 0x1474b39e0 returns 0 (0x1474b3b1b xor eax,eax) and 0x1474b38d0 returns 1. So TimeSync (count(>=5) >= 0) and SyncEvaluation (count(>=18) >= 0) pass at once, and all sends (0x1474b6a60, 0x1474ce590, 0x1474ce080, the NextState message) are skipped. SyncStartMatch still blocks: 0x1474ed840 with a null Strix context (0x14e4c5818) leaves found=0 and value=0. GameTerminating may block too (+0x80c stays 1 unless a callback sets 2).
checks.correction: Offline, the real gates are the 'phaseIndex' check in SyncStartMatch (0x1471c1050) and the PreparingMissionEnd stage in GameTerminating (+0x80c>=2 or +0x804==1). TimeSync and SyncEvaluation are not gates offline. The match clock is set by the host as 0x1474b38d0 defines it (always true offline).

checks.claim: RVNG implications: (1) fill the member-state table +0x210 with the member count at +0x538 so the sync states pass; (2) one peer acts as room owner through StrixManager_+0x1fa; (3) respawn the opponent copy with RespawnAtPoint or +0xbf8; (4) write VictoryScore to GameMode.MissionConfig.
checks.evidence: See the checks above: the member count comes from Strix (0x1474b39e0), not from +0x538. Setting +0x1fa would switch on every network send and the Strix-backed member and owner queries. +0xbf8 with skipMove skips RespawnedPlayer. The victory check reads the WorldSettings MissionConfig.
checks.correction: Staying offline (+0x1fa=0) makes each client host with 0 members, so RVNG only needs to bypass the phaseIndex gate (detour 0x1471c1050 or the SyncStartMatch tick +0xd20) and drive +0x80c or GameTerminating. It should not fake +0x1fa or +0x538. To mirror a respawn, call +0xbf8 with skipMove=false (or RespawnAtPoint) on the copy and be aware that it fires RespawnedPlayer. Write VictoryScore to WorldSettings.MissionSettings.MissionConfig.

missed: StrixManager_+0x1fa is the 'online / in a Strix room' flag, not the room owner. The host test is 0x1474b38d0 (lobby type 0xC8 -> false; +0x1fa==0 -> true; else local member id 0x1474efb30(strix, netmgr+0x520) == 0x1474efc20, the first id of the Strix member list). Survival's COOP2MP.md:261 also calls gm+0x1fa the online flag. Offline, the local member id is 0 and every state, time, finish and PreparingMissionEnd network send is skipped.

Offline gating (static): the member count 0x1474b39e0 returns 0 when +0x1fa==0, so TimeSync (0x1471c6810) and SyncEvaluation (0x1471c8e10) pass at once. The blocking gates are SyncStartMatch's 'phaseIndex' read (0x1471c1050 -> 0x1474ed840; with a null Strix context 0x14e4c5818 it returns not-found and value 0) and GameTerminating (0x1471c8190).

GameTerminating advances only when PreparingMissionEnd stage +0x80c >= 2 or ForcedTerminationState +0x804 == 1 (Aborted). It then waits WaitingRadioInterval (ALiveGameMode +0x3cc, reflected float) of time-in-state (+0x57c), or a CDO value (0x1471d17f0 -> +0xd8) when forced. Stage 2 is written only by callback functors at 0x1471d47a7 and 0x1471d47c4. Stage 3 (timeout, written at 0x1474b9c4b in the online-only network-manager tick) blocks forever. The normal finish path sets only stage 1 (0x1471cb684), so an offline finish may stall here (inferred).

The DM victory check (0x1471df5f0) reads VictoryScore from the level's WorldSettings.MissionSettings.MissionConfig (world+0x30 -> +0x2a0 -> +0x500; poff MissionSettings 0x500), falling back to the ULiveDeathMatchMissionConfig CDO (class 0x1471a4890, +0x110). It does not read GameMode.MissionConfig (+0x530). It compares float scores for EVERY plane in world manager+0x138, so each client ends the match on its own copy of the scores.

+0xc28 (0x1471c01f0) returns -1 for a pawn whose score is <= 0 (or when the top score is <= 0). So a 0-point local player gets DM_MissionFinish rank 0 ('NoRank'), and RankChanged does not fire on the move from -1 (stored in DM+0x828) to a first rank.

0x1474cc700, which counts members at state >= N, is 'jmp 0x15c19a270' into the protected .sbss section. The body is obfuscated (it reads encrypted globals such as 0x14fc5afb4), so a signature on the body is not practical. Hook the thunk or its callers instead.

PreparingMissionEnd (0x1471cb5e0) is sent through the LOCAL PLAYER PLANE's network object (+0xed0, class 0x146ef9b60, 0x1474c69c0), not the game mode's. RecvPreparingMissionEnd always runs 0x1471cb5e0, using the message's flags when the id is not local, and forces termination only when msg+0x14 equals the local member id (0 offline).

Time-up: +0xb30 (0x1471c92f0) is the trigger. The host (0x1474b38d0) additionally sends 0x1474ce590 when online, and every client calls +0xb38 itself. A pure local timeout therefore needs no network message.

In +0xbf8 (0x147d5cd60), the skipMove argument (r9b) also suppresses the teleport, the input-block clear and the RespawnedPlayer EP trigger (0x147d5cf09). The trigger also requires GameMode vfunc +0xb70 true. RespawnAtPoint's sender 0x1474a98e0 sends location and rotation, not a point id.
LoadPlayerPlane tick (0x1471c6450) advances when byte +0x5f1 is ZERO (cmp/je NextState), the reverse of what the report says.

OnGameFinish calls +0xac8 (end-sequence creation, NewObject of 0x146ee7ef0 with vf+0x2b8(3.0f)) and NetworkManager 0x1474b5a30 on every call. Only the rest is guarded by +0x521. The SoloPVP/DM start hook calls ALiveGameMode 0x1471ba2a0 and plays cue 6 (Online's +0xb28 is just jmp 0x1471ba2a0).

Supporting artifacts for this verification (scratch only): <scratchpad>/pvp_research/flow-verify/ (v1.txt vtable diff; d1-d14.txt disassembly; pkg/ re-extracted DT_MissionContents, DT_GameModeScoreCalculationTable, DT_ScoreConstTable, BP_ChronicleDeathMatchGameMode; tools/v1-v7.py).

report.summary: AC8's online PvP doesn't use Unreal replication. Each player plane, game object, game mode and the "system" object owns a native ULiveNetworkBaseObject subclass (no reflected fields or UFUNCTIONs), which talks in Strix-serialized FLiveMessage* classes; there are 146 of them, named "jp.co.soft_gear.strix.server.ext.message.game.FLiveMessage*". On the 2026-11-02 exe (all addresses below are VAs, base 0x140000000) the whole transport goes through two native choke points. Outbound, every game message is stamped by 0x1474a1c90, which writes the network type/id and a synced-clock time, and then sent by 0x1474a2190. That function looks up the Strix room context for channel 0 and is the Live module's only caller of the Strix send 0x14a4379a0 (146 call sites in 85 functions). Inbound, the Strix room-relay and direct-relay notification lambdas call 0x14750b2d0, which hands the message to one router, 0x1474ef630. The router keys on (msg+0x10 type byte << 56 | msg+0x14 id), finds the target network object in a TMap at NS+0x2e0 (NS = GameMode+0x910) and calls the delegates in that object's per-class-id handler map at +0x38. Each network class fills that map in its vtable slot 87 (+0x2b8). The PvP-relevant handlers are on ULiveNetworkGameObject (Damage, DamageClient, Respawn/RequestRespawn, TeleportToRespawnPoint/Request..., ScoreAddition/ScoreUpdate, ObjectAttach, plus Physics/AirCurrent/PostStall/Health state slots at N+0x88..+0x100), on ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane (weapon fire, lock-on, flares, cloud/flare escapes, DestroyedLocation, RespawnTimeEnd, gear, PreparingMissionEnd, input state at N+0x170) and on ULiveNetworkSystemObject (GameTime/RealTime/TimeUp, EvaluationData/List, ResultState, Kick, Cheat, EAC peer data). One authority point matters most. Seventeen message types, among them DamageClient, RequestRespawn, RequestTeleportToRespawnPoint, ScoreUpdate, EvaluationList, RealTime and LatencyResponse, are only ever built by the client's deserializer and never by game code. So they come from Bandai's Strix server extension. The client sends Damage, Respawn, ScoreAddition and EvaluationData, and the victim's owner applies damage only on DamageClient (handler flag 1 → 0x1474aacb0 → local apply 0x147d104a0). This points to server-side validation and aggregation, and nothing in the client holds those rules. Survival's COOP2MP already drives a real remote ALivePlayerPlane (role 2) by writing straight into the network object's state messages (N+0x98 physics, N+0x170 input) before RemoteUpdate, and it replays weapons through the native RemoteFire and select/arm/launch calls. It never routes anything through the message router, and it carries no native damage, death, respawn, score or result messages. Hits on real planes are refused by role, and real planes are never destroyed. For RVNG, a protocol-level Strix emulator (a) isn't realistic. Survival's offline feed (b) is proven for flight and weapon visuals only. The most native workable route is (c), and only parts of it have been checked statically: give both planes registered network objects in an offline level, capture the game's own outgoing FLiveMessages at 0x1474a2190, inject the peer's at router 0x1474ef630, and have RVNG's link stand in for the few server-made messages. All of this needs a native (C++) module, because none of it is reachable from UE4SS Lua RegisterHook.

findings.finding: 146 FLiveMessage* type names (UTF-16, 0x14bfcb070..0x14bfce200) are referenced from exactly one function, 0x145295560..0x1452990ac. For each type it calls that type's type-info getter, reads the class id at [getter()+0x48] and maps the id to the name; this looks like the traffic-log/name registry. The same 146 types exist as Strix Java class names 'jp.co.soft_gear.strix.server.ext.message.game.FLiveMessage*' (ASCII 0x14bfc57e0..). Each message object's vtable slot 0 is a jmp to its getter, so the class id is read at runtime and never needs hard-coding. findings.topic: FLiveMessageBase layout and network ids
findings.finding: The stamp function 0x1474a1c90(N, TSharedPtr<msg>) writes msg+0x10 (u8) = N+0x2f (the network type byte), msg+0x14 (u32) = N+0x28 (the network id), and msg+0x08 = time from the synced clock (0x147907550 singleton offsets + QPC 0x147907660). On receive, the router writes the sender into msg+0x1c. The network key is (type<<56 | id). This matches the remote spawn's NetworkObject+0x28 = id | 0x200000000000000 (type 2 = ELiveNetworkType::Player). Enum ELiveNetworkType: Invalid 0, System 1, Player 2, Npc 3, Bot 4, Unit 5, GameMode 6, SimplePlayerResponse 7, Lobby 32, Guild 33, Centurion 34. RemoteFire turns msg+0x08 into latency = min((now - t) * 1e-7, 3) s, so the time unit is 100 ns ticks.

findings.topic: Network object classes and handler registration (vtable slot 87)
findings.finding: The ULiveNetwork* classes add exactly one virtual to UObject's: slot 87 (+0x2b8), which registers message handlers. The base (vtable 0x14c874958) has 0x1474a1b90. It adds the object to NS+0x2e0 (TMap<uint64 key, TWeakObjectPtr>, keyed by N+0x28) where NS = World->AuthorityGameMode(+0x1d8)->+0x910. Subclass registrations: ULiveNetworkGameObject vt 0x14c871d08 -> 0x1474a7c70; ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane vt 0x14c86fe38 -> 0x1474c34f0 (calls the GameObject one first); ULiveNetworkGameMode vt 0x14c8718d8 -> 0x1474a5730; ULiveNetworkSystemObject vt 0x14c870c68 -> 0x1474ccc30; ULiveNetworkPVPVEGameMode vt 0x14c870168 -> 0x1474c97a0; ULiveNetworkResultObject vt 0x14c8704b8 -> 0x1474ca400; ULiveNetworkAircraftSelector vt 0x14c874cc0 -> 0x14749a950; ULiveNetworkSimplePlayerResponseObject vt 0x14c871020 -> 0x1474cb400. Handlers go into a per-object TMap<int32 classId, TSharedPtr<handler list>> at N+0x38, through 0x1474a1d70 (get or add), 0x1474a1e90 (add) and 0x1474a1f10 (a state-message slot with two delegates). Each delegate keeps a weak pointer to the object (+0x18 index, +0x1c serial) and a thunk (+0x20). Class names were matched to vtables through the name pointer just before each vtable plus each class's registered message set; the player-plane one is confirmed because its ExplosiveWeaponFire thunk 0x1474c7200 calls RemoteFire.
sources: python -I mx.py xref 0x1474a1d70 / 0x1474a1e90 0x1474a1f10 (the callers are the registration functions)
