findings.topic: Inbound seam: Strix relay -> router -> object
findings.finding: 0x1474eee50(NS, channel) binds Strix room-context notifications (Strix SDK fns 0x14a49adc0, 0x14a49aee0, ...) to lambdas. Two of the lambda vtables (0x14cb6a9b8, 0x14cb6aa18; room relay and direct relay, inferred) hold 0x14750b2d0, which calls the router 0x1474ef630(NS, sender, TSharedPtr<FLiveMessageBase>). The router checks IsA FLiveMessageBase, puts the sender in msg+0x1c, forces type 1 for NpcRandomLotteryResult, builds the key and looks it up in NS+0x2e0. When it finds the object it dispatches through the +0x38 handler map. When it doesn't, it checks for Damage (0x1474b8a50) and Error (0x1474b9080). NS+0x1fa is the online flag: the NS ctor 0x1474ec410 clears it, and StartOnline 0x1474ee290 / 0x1474ee2f0 (called from 0x1474ed141) bind the relay handlers and set it to 1. The 'ULiveNetworkManager::Tick : received message was too old' / 'room server connection closed' strings exist (0x14cb67ec0 etc.) but no code references them by rip-relative lea or absolute pointer.

findings.topic: Outbound seam: one send function
findings.finding: 0x1474a2190(?, TSharedPtr<msg>) reads the global 0x14e4c5818 (the Strix client object, stored by 0x1452935d4 at 0x1452936ca), looks up channel 0's room context in its +0x60 std::map, and calls Strix 0x14a4379a0(roomCtx, 1, &msg, ...). The call returns quietly when there is no global or no room context. It is the Live module's only caller of 0x14a4379a0 (the other callers are lobby code at 0x1452xxxxx) and has 146 call sites in 85 functions: every player-plane sender (0x1474c4fed..0x1474c69c0), game-object senders (SendDamage 0x1474a9360, Respawn 0x1474a98e0, TeleportToRespawnPoint, ScoreAddition), game-mode senders (0x1474a6090..0x1474a6b10) and system-object senders (0x1474cdb90..0x1474cee50). Offline, the game's own senders that only need a network object (for example RespawnAt sends Respawn when plane+0xed0 is set) end in this function and are dropped, because no room context exists (inferred).

findings.topic: Messages the client receives but never builds (server-originated)
findings.finding: These message vtables are referenced in code only by their deserializer factory (the type-info 'Create', data-referenced only), never by game code, and their getters have no other users. The client can receive them but never sends them: DamageClient, RequestRespawn, RequestTeleportToRespawnPoint, ScoreUpdate, EvaluationList, RealTime, LatencyResponse, SetObjectInformation, EventHash, NpcRandomLotteryResult, RespawnRescueResult, MissionRewardUser, ChangeBot, OperateBot, PVPVETicket, PVPVETargetHealth, EntityUpdateResult. Each has a client-sent counterpart: Damage->DamageClient, Respawn->RequestRespawn, TeleportToRespawnPoint->RequestTeleportToRespawnPoint, ScoreAddition->ScoreUpdate, EvaluationData->EvaluationList, LatencyCheck->LatencyResponse, RespawnRescueTry->RespawnRescueResult, NpcRandomLotteryData->NpcRandomLotteryResult, EntityUpdate->EntityUpdateResult. So the Strix server extension ('server.ext.message.game') validates client reports and answers with derived messages; ELiveNetworkCheatType (client_damage, client_player_location, client_weapon_cooltime/ammo/id/location, client_eac_kick) fits server-side checks. The pairing is reasoned, not read.
sources: python -I dref.py 0x14bfd7bb0 0x14bfd7070 0x14bfd70b0 0x14bfd74d0 0x14bfd7030 (one code ref each, inside 0x1452b2c50/0x1452b3f10/0x1452b40d0/0x1452b5e10/0x1452b3d50)

findings.topic: Damage authority online
findings.finding: In the game object's damage path (11-02) the code reads NS = 0x1474ae240(obj) (GetWorld->AuthorityGameMode+0x910) and tests NS+0x1fa at 0x147d1037d and 0x147d10ea1. Online, a hit is applied locally (0x147d104a0) only when obj+0x739 is set and 0x1474b38d0(obj) says this machine owns it: the owner member index (+0x520) is compared through NS (0x1474efb30 vs 0x1474efc20). Offline, 0x1474b38d0 always answers true. Otherwise the shooter's game calls 0x147d1af10 -> SendDamage 0x1474a9360, which builds FLiveMessageDamage (vtable 0x14bfd70d0, factory 0x1474bbec0), stamps it with the TARGET's network id and sends it. On receive: Damage (0x1474aa990) -> 0x1474aacb0(N, msg, 0), feedback only (0x147d1b070, no health change). DamageClient (0x1474aaae0) copies fields +0x10,+0x14,+0x20,+0x24,+0x28,+0x29,+0x2a,+0x2c,+0x30,+0x31 into a new Damage and calls 0x1474aacb0(N, msg, 1); with flag 1 the owner applies through 0x147d104a0. COOP2MP field names for these offsets are AttackerNetworkTypeId/Id, WeaponId, Health, Killed (the exact mapping is not traced). Before any of this, CanBeDamagedBy uses role bytes: on the victim's game a role-2 attacker is refused, so a player's hit is decided on the shooter's game and applied by the victim's owner game after the server's DamageClient.

findings.topic: Respawn, death location and score
findings.finding: RespawnAt 0x147d18c80(obj, pointIndex, flag) gets the point's location and rotation (0x147d188e0). If the plane has a network object (+0xed0) it sends FLiveMessageRespawn (0x1474a98e0), then calls vslot +0xbf8 (the PP respawn 0x147d5cd60: teleport, SetActive, OnRestored, RespawnedPlayer trigger; health not touched). The RequestRespawn handler, for a role-2 target only, calls RespawnAt(msg+0x20 index, msg+0x24 != 0). The RequestTeleportToRespawnPoint handler (role 2) calls 0x147d18e20, which also sends via 0x1474a9ab0 and vslots 0xc40/0xc00. The DestroyedLocation handler (role 2) moves the copy (0x143fd2150). ScoreAddition is sent by the game object (0x1474a9c77) and handled with owner vslot +0xc10. ScoreUpdate (server-originated) goes to vslot +0xc18. TeamScoreAddition belongs to the game mode. Reflected state: ALiveGameMode.ScoreRankList, BaseRespawnTime, TeamGroupList, NetworkObject (ULiveNetworkGameMode*); ALiveDeathMatchGameMode.RankingForPlayers (TArray<ALivePlayerPlane*>); ALiveTeamDeathMatchGameMode.AlphaRankList/BravoRankList.

findings.topic: Lock-on, evasion, gun: PvP-critical messages Survival does not carry
findings.finding: The LockedTarget handler (0x1474c6cd0) resolves the target through NS (GetNetManager 0x147ece910 + lookup 0x1474bbfe0) and, for a role-2 plane, calls 0x147d61610 (the remote plane's lock; this is how a victim gets the lock warning, inferred). EscapeByFlare (0x1474c8140) and EscapeInClouds (0x1474c7ff0) read plane +0x18a8; this is how the victim's game reports that it dodged a shooter's missile, inferred, effect not traced. HoldingMachineGunButton sets weapons +0x311 (COOP2MP). SpecialWeaponArmed (0x1474c82b0) selects and arms (0x147f4e940 / 0x147f51e70). Survival replays launches, flares, gun trigger, gear and ESM/ECM. It sends no lock, escape, hit (ExplosiveWeaponHit) or SpecialWeaponArmed messages.

findings.topic: What Survival COOP2MP injects (proven in game)
findings.finding: (1) The remote spawn steps (deferred SpawnActor of the airframe class, ALiveNetworkDummyController Possess, vslot +0xc60 network object, role byte +0xed8 = 2, loadout 0x147d4ad20-equivalent and bytes +0xfa0/+0xfa1, paint +0xfa4/+0xfb8/+0xfc8, name +0x6e8 / ObjName +0x6d8, FinishSpawning), with addresses read from the remote spawn's own code. (2) A detour on RemoteUpdate that writes the pose, State and speed into *(N+0x98) (+0x20 dir, +0x2c int3 cm, +0x38 rot deg, +0x44 State, +0x48 speed) and the stick and flags into *(N+0x170) (+0x08..+0x1c, +0x20 flags) before the game reads them. It never pushes a message through the router, and N+0x170 must be treated as a TSharedPtr (writing inline crashed Quit Mission). (3) Afterburner plane+0x39d0 before the surface update, and gear through both flight engines. (4) Weapons: PlaneWeaponsFired capture, the native RemoteFire with a hand-built {ExplosiveWeaponFire*, ctrl}, laser and ESM/ECM via select/arm/launch (FwLaunchDirect), flares via FireFlares, gun via weapons+0x311, a LaunchWeapon hook that supplies the target (offline the network-id map is empty), and a weapon-table bounds check before replays. (5) ESM/ECM: other real planes set to role 1 around the plane electronic update. (6) Health display: HealthInternal written, MinHealth floored. Its own transport (Steam P2P or UDP, 30 Hz P packets with a 13-byte flight block, reliable Lua 'fx' shots) replaces Strix completely.

findings.topic: What Survival does NOT carry (and why its way stops there)
findings.finding: Survival carries no FLiveMessage at all: everything goes in its own packets or by writing memory. Damage: hits on a role-2 real plane reach the player plane's damage and are refused (T1e: kind 2, 40 dmg, returned 0). Damage whose cause is a role-2 plane is refused too (the 0.73.20 'ghosts'), so Survival deals its own damage with no cause. Death: a real plane is never destroyed mid-level (0.73.12 crash: some system keeps a raw pointer; it is floored at 1 HP). Respawn: Survival's own hide/show DOWN state, not RespawnAt/RequestRespawn. Score, kills and results: Survival Lua (KILL.read), not ScoreAddition/ScoreUpdate/Evaluation*. Not carried either: lock-on and lock warnings, flare and cloud escapes, missile hit events, the game-mode state and timers.

findings.topic: Network system present offline
findings.finding: The object at GameMode+0x910 (NS: router owner, id map +0x2e0, online flag +0x1fa) exists in Survival's offline level. RemoteFire dereferences it unchecked, and Survival checks the getter and then replayed launches successfully in T4a/T4b. COOP2MP also reports the network-id map is empty offline, which is why LaunchWeapon is hooked to supply the target. ALiveGameMode.NetworkObject (ULiveNetworkGameMode*) is a separate, small object: its ctor 0x146f00790 only sets the vtable.

findings.topic: Remote player spawn caller chain (11-02)
findings.finding: The remote spawn is 0x1471b84f0(owner, playerIndex, planeClass). It is called from 0x1471b9330 and 0x1471b95f2; 0x1471b9330 is called from 0x1471b7430. These are most likely the online game mode's LoadPlayerPlane/SpawnPlayerPlane states (ELiveOnlineGameModeState); not traced further. Player data comes from the session (COOP.md), which offline has no Chronicle/Strix match.

findings.topic: Reflection reach for UE4SS Lua
findings.finding: None of the PvP machinery is reflected. ULiveNetwork* classes have no UPROPERTY or UFUNCTION (except ULiveNetworkManager's KickRoomMember callbacks and the ULiveNetworkResultManager map). ALiveDeathMatchGameMode / ALiveSoloPVPGameMode / ALiveOnlineGameMode declare no UFUNCTIONs. FLiveMessage* are not USTRUCTs. RVNG's main.lua HOOKS ('/Script/TODO.MultiplayerGameMode:OnMatchStarted', 'AircraftPawn:ReceiveDamage', ...) and GAME.createRoom/joinRoom therefore have no native counterparts that RegisterHook can reach. RVNG needs a native module, as Survival's main.dll is.

rvngImplications: Drop the Strix room design: GAME.createRoom/joinRoom (main.lua:41-43, GAME_INTEGRATION.md:20) need Bandai login, the Chronicle matchmaker and Strix room servers, which modded offline clients can't reach. The two pilots meet over RVNG's own link and load the same offline level.

RVNG needs a native module (UE4SS C++ mod or a Survival-style main.dll). The network objects, handlers, router and send function are native C++ with no reflection, so Lua RegisterHook placeholders like '/Script/TODO.AircraftPawn:ReceiveDamage' can't reach them.

Option (a), emulating Strix servers at the protocol level, is not realistic: proprietary master and room protocol, auth tokens from Bandai/Chronicle login, EAC peer data (FLiveMessageEasyAntiCheatPeerData), possibly Oodle (UStrixNetworkFacade.IsOodleEnable). The server-extension rules behind DamageClient, ScoreUpdate, RequestRespawn and EvaluationList aren't in the exe at all.

Option (b), Survival's way, is proven for flight, gear, afterburner, missiles, laser, ESM/ECM, flares, gun, loadout, paint and name. Used alone, damage, death, respawn and score would be RVNG-made logic, which is not the native PvP path. Reuse it as the fallback and as the flight layer.

Option (c), recommended and staged, uses the game's own messages over RVNG's link in an offline level. (1) Give your own plane a network object through vslot +0xc60, as the remote spawn does, set a role-3 'your plane' value as Online Mode does, and register both planes' network objects through vslot +0x2b8 (slot 87), so both are in NS+0x2e0 and their +0x38 handler maps are filled. Use the same network id on both machines: the peer's copy must carry the owner's id | 2<<56. (2) Detour the single send function 0x1474a2190 (11-02) to capture every FLiveMessage the game builds: weapon fire, lock, flares, escapes, Damage, Respawn, ScoreAddition, DestroyedLocation, state messages. (3) Ship them and inject them on the peer with the router 0x1474ef630(NS, sender, TSharedPtr<msg>), so the game's own handlers run (RemoteFire, lock warning, escape, respawn of the copy, score). (4) RVNG's link plays the server extension for the few server-made types: the victim's game turns a received Damage aimed at its own plane into DamageClient (fields copied 1:1, as 0x1474aaae0 shows); Respawn becomes RequestRespawn and TeleportToRespawnPoint becomes RequestTeleportToRespawnPoint; ScoreAddition is summed into ScoreUpdate; EvaluationData into EvaluationList, if results are wanted.

Serialisation for (c): either call Strix's own serializer through each message's type-info object (the 0x14bfd4xxx-0x14bfd6xxx vtables; Create is data-referenced at, for example, 0x14bfd50b0; the serialize/deserialize slots are not yet located), or hand-marshal the roughly 25 PvP types. Read class ids at runtime as [getter()+0x48], with getters found through the registry function 0x145295560 that names all 146 types; don't hard-code ids or addresses.

Stamp injected messages as the game does (0x1474a1c90): msg+0x10 type, +0x14 id, +0x08 time in 100 ns ticks from the receiving game's clock (0x147907550/0x147907660). Otherwise RemoteFire's latency becomes wrong (capped at 3 s) and the 'message too old' drop may apply.

Damage authority, the native way: a hit is decided on the shooter's game (CanBeDamagedBy: a role-2 target needs a role-3 attacker, so set your own plane to role 3 rather than offline role 1) and applied by the victim's own game. With NS+0x1fa = 0 offline, TakeDamage applies hits locally to the copy, so RVNG must either take the online branch in a targeted way (0x147d1037d / 0x147d10ea1 gate -> 0x147d1af10 -> SendDamage 0x1474a9360) or catch PP damage 0x147d49d30 on the role-2 copy and emit the native Damage. Don't set NS+0x1fa = 1 globally: ownership checks (0x1474b38d0 -> 0x1474efb30/0x1474efc20) then need Strix room-member tables.

Never destroy a live remote ALivePlayerPlane mid-level (Survival hard rule and 0.73.12 crash). Use the native respawn (RespawnAt 0x147d18c80 / vslot +0xbf8) and DestroyedLocation on the copy rather than despawn and respawn.

Both pilots must run the identical exe (message layouts, class ids, 'Old' message variants). Gate on the exe build hash. Every raw VA moved in the 11-02 patch (about -0x106e0 to -0x14000), while struct offsets and vtable slots held. Find functions by signature, by vtable slot from the class's CDO (UE4SS FindObject 'LiveNetworkPlayerPlane' etc. -> vtable -> slot 87), or by anchors such as 'only Live caller of the Strix send' and 'only caller of the router'.
blockers: Several message types are made only by Bandai's Strix server extension: DamageClient, RequestRespawn, RequestTeleportToRespawnPoint, ScoreUpdate, EvaluationList, RealTime, LatencyResponse and others. The rules that make them (validation, score amounts, respawn timing, result list format) are not in the client, so RVNG must reimplement that server logic and it can't be checked against official servers.

No Strix servers, Chronicle matchmaker or EAC for modded clients. The online game mode's network states (WaitingNetworkInitialize, TimeSync, SyncStartMatch, SyncEvaluation) and session player data presumably depend on them (not traced). Running ALiveDeathMatchGameMode itself offline is unproven.

Message serialisation isn't solved: no reflected layout, and Strix serialize/deserialize entry points aren't located. Hand marshalling needs per-type RE of ~25 types; only Damage's field offsets and some weapon and physics layouts are known.

Network-object registration and ids offline are unproven: whether vslot +0x2b8 runs offline, whether the local plane has a network object offline, and how member and owner ids (obj+0x520, NS member tables) must be filled for 0x1474b38d0.

No address here is exercised by RVNG yet, and all of them are from the 2026-11-02 build. Any game patch moves them, and changed message formats would break wire compatibility between pilots on different builds.
openQuestions: Offline outbound test: in an offline level, give your plane a network object (vslot +0xc60 as the remote spawn does) and set role 3. Hook 0x1474a2190 and log each message's class id (read via getter+0x48, named via the 0x145295560 map) while you fly, fire each weapon, flare, lock and take damage. Which FLiveMessages does the game build offline unprompted?

Registration test: call the network object's vslot +0x2b8 on your plane and on a Survival-style remote copy, then dump NS+0x2e0 (TMap count at +0x2e8 vs +0x314) and N+0x38. Are both objects in the map and their handler lists filled?

Inbound test: take a captured ExplosiveWeaponFire from your plane, re-stamp it with the copy's id, type 2 and the current clock, and pass it to router 0x1474ef630(NS, fake sender, TSharedPtr). Does the copy launch the weapon through the native handler 0x1474c7200 -> RemoteFire with no Survival replay code, and is the target resolved from the NS map?

Damage test: with your plane at role 3 and the copy at role 2, hit the copy with a missile. Does CanBeDamagedBy pass, and with NS+0x1fa = 0 does the copy's health drop locally? Then build an FLiveMessageDamageClient-equivalent (fields +0x20..+0x31 copied from a captured Damage) aimed at your own plane's network id and route it. Does 0x1474aacb0(flag 1) apply the damage, kill credit and death natively?
Field mapping test: log a captured FLiveMessageDamage's bytes +0x20..+0x31 against the known attacker, weapon and damage to name AttackerNetworkTypeId/Id, WeaponId, Health and Killed.

Respawn test: on the peer, deliver RequestRespawn (msg+0x20 respawn-point index, +0x24 flag) to the opponent's copy (role 2). Does RespawnAt 0x147d18c80 move and reactivate the copy using the deathmatch level's respawn points? Which level data holds those points offline?

Find the Strix serializer: disassemble the type-info vtable family (for example 0x14bfd50b8 for RequestRespawn, 0x14bfd5028 for Damage) to locate Serialize/Deserialize slots. Could RVNG serialise any FLiveMessage generically with the game's own code?

Census of other Strix calls: list every call from the Live module into the Strix SDK range (0x14a4xxxxx..) besides 0x14a4379a0 and the relay binding in 0x1474eee50 (room-member queries, SyncTime). That shows what else the online game mode needs before it would run with Strix stubbed.

missed: The network system's owner is the game instance, not the game mode. World+0x1d8 is OwningGameInstance: it is class-checked with 0x146e2f590 = ULiveGameInstance::StaticClass, and Survival runtime/survival_rt.c:56 defines WORLD_GAME_INSTANCE 0x1D8. UE FPropertyParams in the exe give these ULiveGameInstance offsets: SoundManager +0x908, StrixManager_ +0x910 (ULiveStrixManager = router owner, id map +0x2e0, online flag +0x1fa; params 0x14c6ffe90), MatchmakerManager_ +0x918, StrixMessenger_ +0x920, NetworkManager_ +0x928 (ULiveNetworkManager; params 0x14c6ffdd0), NetworkP2P_ +0x930 (params 0x14c6ffcd0), NetworkResultManager_ +0x960 (params 0x14c6ffb90). The getters are 0x147ece910 (+0x910) and 0x147ece7f0 (+0x928). Because these objects live on the GameInstance, they persist across level loads. Evidence: seam-verify/propoff.py and scname.py.

0x1474b38d0 is a ULiveNetworkManager-level host test, not a per-object ownership test. Every call site loads GameInstance+0x928 (0x147d10392, 0x147d10eb6, 0x147d1af7f, 0x1474aaf05, 0x1474ab2fd, 0x1474a69a9, 0x1471b7a03, 0x147dba6c4, 0x1473e4596). It passes NM+0x520 to the static Strix-client queries 0x1474efb30 (-> 0x1452947b0) and 0x1474efc20 (-> 0x145294cc0, first element), both on the global 0x14e4c5818. The local apply of a received DamageClient is gated by this test (0x1474aaf05 -> 0x147d104a0, else feedback 0x147d1b070). SendDamage receives the result as its third argument (0x147d1afa0). Online damage therefore looks host-applied, with Health state slot sync at GO+0xf8 (handler thunk 0x1474aa800) the probable way other games learn health (inferred).

Network objects are created and registered only online. The game object's setup chunk 0x147d13de3 tests StrixManager+0x1fa at 0x147d13e7c, then calls vslot +0xc60 (create N, PP 0x147d5e650), +0xc58 (PP 0x147d5e5c0) and +0xc68 (PP 0x147d5e740, which calls N's slot 87 and, for non-role-2 planes, 0x1474c4380 with plane+0x2268). This is the native reason the id map is empty offline, and +0xc68 is the native registration entry that RVNG should use instead of raw slot 87.

The 'message too old' drop is live code. ULiveNetworkManager's tick (chunk 0x1474ad641) copies L'ULiveNetworkManager::Tick : received message was too old' (0x14cb67ec0) with movaps at 0x1474adb26 and leas 'client error : received message was too old' (0x14cb67f40) at 0x1474adb85 when 0x1474ba280(NM) returns 0; that check walks a sparse set at NM+0x6a8 (not fully traced). The same tick tests NM+0x4c9 and StrixManager +0x1f9/+0x1fa. The report's lea-only xref scan missed this.

There is a third Strix start variant, 0x1474ee380: it calls 0x1474eee50 and sets word [StrixManager+0x1f9] = 0x0101. 0x1474ee2f0 also branches on +0x30 to call 0x1474ee670 instead of 0x1474eee50. The meaning of +0x1f9 (maybe a P2P or offline-host mode) is untraced.

With the global Strix client 0x14e4c5818 null, 0x1474efb30 returns 0 (zeroed out struct) and 0x1474efc20 returns 0 (ebp=0), so the host test passes even when the online flag is set. Whether the client object exists in an offline session is unknown: it is stored at 0x1452936ca (0x1452935d4) and 0x145293b55 (0x1452939f0, called from 0x1451f6f40, 0x14528c9e0 and 0x1474ed7e0).

ALiveGameMode.NetworkObject is at GameMode+0x738 (params 0x14cb3a8e0). Other offsets: ScoreRankList +0x718, AIActionEventManager +0x730, CanopyReflectionNS +0x740, ALiveDeathMatchGameMode.RankingForPlayers +0x830, ALiveGameObject.NetworkObject +0xed0, ULiveNetworkManager.NetworkObject (ULiveNetworkSystemObject*) +0x4c0. The report gave no offsets for these reflected PvP members.

47 message types, not 17, are built only by their deserializer factory. Besides the PvP ones, they include AIFCSLockedTarget, AIFCSLockedLocation, AIHoldingMachineGunButton, AITrackingLocation, AIPrivateSync, AIInfo, ALCMLottery, StaurosLottery, SystemObjectHelios, Error and LogOutput. EntityUpdateResult is not one of them: three code places reference its vtable. Evidence: seam-verify/msg_vt_users.txt.

FLiveMessageGameModeState is a SystemObject state message: its vtable 0x14bfd7570 is used by the SystemObject ctor 0x15c1a05f0 (in the protected section) and the sender 0x1474cdb90. No handler table registers it, so the game-mode state machine is synced through the SystemObject.

The game has its own ULiveNetworkP2P (GameInstance.NetworkP2P_ +0x930, wide name 'ULiveNetworkP2P' at 0x14c8781c8, no reflected members). It is untraced and is a possible native P2P seam that should be checked before designing a substitute.

More network classes exist than the report lists: ULiveNetworkAIGameObject and its AI subclasses (AIPlane, AIHeli and others, relevant to DM bots), ULiveNetworkUnit, ULiveNetworkCoopGameMode (parent of CompetitiveCoop and EmergencyCall*), ULiveNetworkDebugCommand, and the exe-only LiveNetworkAvatarObject, LiveNetworkCenturionObject and LiveNetworkGuildObject. Their registration functions (callers of 0x1474a1d70/0x1474a1e90/0x1474a1f10 such as 0x147494ee0, 0x147497a20, 0x1474a4bc0, 0x1474cc4e0 and 0x1474d1690) were not mapped.

Unrouted messages go to ULiveNetworkManager: when the router finds no object it fetches GameInstance+0x928 via 0x147ece7f0 and calls 0x1474b8a50 for Damage or 0x1474b9080 for Error. The Error check runs when the message fails IsA FLiveMessageBase.

Five more senders call 0x1474a2190: 0x14813a280, 0x14813a570, 0x14813a750, 0x14813a930 and 0x14813ab60 (called from 0x1480ed267, 0x148119b85, 0x148118930, 0x1481185c1 and 0x148100bb1). They also stamp via 0x1474a1c90. Their classes are unidentified.

The sig-found addresses in the drift table are verified on the 11-02 build by Survival's runtime log of 2026-11-16 (build/autotest/runs/20261116_192741_claude/survival_logs/AC8SurvivalMode_2026-11-16_19-27-49.log: 'player plane damage: hooked at 147D49D30', 'network manager 147ECE910'), so they deserve 'verified' rather than 'static'. All scripts used for this check are in <scratchpad>/pvp_research/seam-verify/ (vsigs.py, propoff.py, scname.py, regmap.py, msgvt.py, getters.txt, msg_vt_users.txt, sigscan.txt).

report.summary: The game does not decide who is an enemy with a flag on the plane. It uses one native test: ALiveGameObject virtual slot +0x8d8, at 0x147d0ba90 in the 2026-11-02 exe. That test calls two objects hostile when their ELiveFaction bytes (ALiveGameObject.Faction, +0x3b2) differ, unless both factions sit in one FLiveTeamGroup of ALiveGameMode.TeamGroupList (+0x3a8). It has one extra rule for AI objects with an UnidentifiedType, which matters only when a player plane is one of the two. Deathmatch makes every human an enemy by giving each pilot their own faction. WD_DM has 8 starts (Start_Alpha0..Start_Zulu0, factions 1..8) with 5 respawn points each, DT_MissionContents row I_EM_17 is 8 teams of 1, and BP_ChronicleDeathMatchGameMode leaves TeamGroupList unset. Team Deathmatch uses Alpha(1) against Bravo(2) with 2 teams of 4, so teammates share a faction. Online, the faction of each player plane comes from the room. A game-mode virtual (0x1471c5a50) goes through LiveActorManager.CachedPlayerPlanes and looks each plane up by the FString at plane+0x2200 in a native member map of ULiveNetworkManager (GameInstance+0x928, map at +0x4d0, entry = faction byte plus member index). It writes Faction and builds the callsign 'Online_Hud_OnlineMissionCallsign_<Faction>_<index>_Name'. No in-match Strix message carries a player's faction. When the game is not in a Strix room (ULiveStrixManager+0x1fa == 0), the caller 0x1471b3a00 sets every cached player plane to Alpha. That is exactly why Survival's role-2 real-plane copy shows as ALLY: same faction, so not hostile. The AI target search calls the +0x8d8 test directly. The player's lock list (TargetSelectionComponent TargetCandidates/AllyGameObjects), the HUD box (ALLY/ENEMY text, HUD_ColorHostile/Friendly) and the minimap icons (OtherPlayer vs RaivalPlayer) all depend on the same side split, but their code sits in unreadable protected code, so that link is inferred. Whether a hit counts is a separate check: the network role byte +0xed8 (1 offline/local, 2 remote, 3 local-online). Online, a player's shots are decided on the shooter's game and the victim's game gets Damage/Health messages. Flares are reported back with EscapeByFlare {EscapeNum, PlayerMissileEscapeNum, DoubleLockonEscapeNum}, and lock state travels as LockedTarget/SelectedTarget. For player against player, the damage-rate tables are the same in the campaign and online versions (Fighter 110%, Multirole 100%, Attacker 85%, Electronic 100% against player-plane columns 01-04). No PvP-only ban list for special weapons or parts was found. So RVNG should spawn the opponent as a real role-2 player plane and give the two pilots distinct factions (host Alpha, guest Bravo on both PCs). It must set them again after the offline Alpha reset, and it must carry hits, flare escapes and lock state over its own link, because offline the game refuses role-2 hits.

findings.topic: The game's native hostility test (who is an enemy)
findings.finding: 0x147d0ba90 (exe of 2026-11-02) = ALiveGameObject virtual at vtable slot +0x8d8, signature bool(this=a, other=b, ALiveGameMode* gm). Logic: (1) a==b -> false. (2) If a or b answers true at vf+0xb28 (AI: UnidentifiedType != None) and a or b is a player plane (vf+0xaa0): hostile unless either's vf+0xb30 (UnidentifiedType) == 4 (Ally). (3) If gm is not garbage (flags bit 30 clear): for each FLiveTeamGroup in gm->TeamGroupList (+0x3a8 data, +0x3b0 count, stride 0x18, Factions TArray at +0x8): if both factions are in one group -> false. (4) return a->Faction(+0x3b2) != b->Faction. Faction None vs None is not hostile; Other(9) is hostile to everyone. In the ALivePlayerPlane vtable 0x14cbef168 (ctor LEA at 0x147d38454): +0x8d8 = 0x147d0ba90, +0xaa0 = 'mov al,1; ret', +0xb28/+0xb30 = 'xor al,al'. So for two player planes the result is purely faction plus TeamGroupList.

findings.topic: How the game assigns a player plane's faction (online), and why offline everyone is Alpha
findings.finding: 0x1471c5a50 is a virtual in 6 vtables. For every plane in ULiveActorManager.CachedPlayerPlanes (+0x138) it calls 0x1474b6700(NetworkManager_ = ULiveGameInstance+0x928, &plane+0x2200 (FString player id), &faction, &list, &index). That function reads a native TMap at NetworkManager+0x4d0 (pair stride 0x38: FString key, u8 faction at +0x10, TArray at +0x18, int32 member index at +0x28). It then writes plane+0x3b2 (and children) and calls 0x147d3f0c0(plane, list, index). Online, 0x147d3f0c0 builds the callsign text 'Online_Hud_OnlineMissionCallsign_%s_%d_Name' from the ELiveFaction name and index into plane+0x2220, and writes callsign FString +0x6e8. 0x1471b3a00 (slot +0xa70 of vtable 0x14c7013a8; the same vtable's +0x268 is ProcessEvent-like) first calls 0x1471c5a50. If ULiveStrixManager (GameInstance+0x910) byte +0x1fa == 0, i.e. not in an online room, it then sets every cached player plane's Faction = 1 (Alpha) with children and calls 0x147d3f0c0(plane, {}, 1). The Strix message catalogue has no player faction/team message: the only 'Faction' field belongs to FLiveMessageAceBattleNpcData, and 'TeamId' only to FLiveDebugMessageMatchingSet. Factions come from matchmaking/room data, not in-match traffic.

findings.topic: Network role checks and who decides a hit
findings.finding: The ALivePlayerPlane vtable has +0xc40/+0xc48/+0xc50 = role byte +0xed8 ==3 / ==2 / ==1 (0x146db27d0/e0/f0, current build). Role values: offline every local plane is 1; online your own plane is 3 and a remote player 2. Pre-patch RE (COOP2MP.md:255-266, checked in code): CanBeDamagedBy refuses a role-2 attacker, refuses AI hitting a role-2 target, and lets a role-2 target be hit only by a role-3 attacker. So a player's shot is decided on the shooter's game; online a non-host only reports it (SendDamage), with FLiveMessageDamage {AttackerNetworkId, AttackerNetworkTypeId, WeaponId, Health}, DamageClient {Killed}, Health, ExplosiveWeaponHit. In game (T1e and the 0.73.19 'ghosts'), hits on a role-2 copy reach the player-plane damage and return 0, and damage whose attacker is a role-2 plane is refused.

rvngImplications: Spawn the opponent as a real ALivePlayerPlane through the game's remote-spawn path: role byte +0xed8 = 2, ALiveNetworkDummyController, ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane, their loadout lists. Survival's COOP2MP spawn shows this works offline. Do not use an AI stand-in: only a player plane is classed OtherPlayer/EnemyPlayer, shown with the Rival minimap icon and handled by the remote-fire, flare and gear handlers.

Give the two pilots different factions the way Deathmatch does: host = Alpha(1), guest = Bravo(2), the same on both PCs so spawn points (Start_Alpha0/Start_Bravo0, Respawn_Alpha0-4/Respawn_Bravo0-4 in WD_DM) and kill credit agree. Use the native SetFaction(plane, f) (0x147d0b980 in the 2026-11-02 build; find it by signature, not address) so attached child objects follow, or write the reflected LiveGameObject.Faction. Leave ALiveGameMode.TeamGroupList empty.

Re-apply the factions after the game's own assignment. 0x1471b3a00 sets every cached player plane to Alpha whenever the game is not in a Strix room. Do it after spawn, after every respawn, and after any new plane registers. A one-byte compare of +0x3b2 per plane per second, with a re-set if changed, is cheap. Do NOT set ULiveStrixManager+0x1fa or other online flags to get the native assignment: they also switch the damage path to report-only (SendDamage).

For RVNG's isOpponent/isLocal: a pawn is the opponent if it is an ALivePlayerPlane with role byte +0xed8 == 2 (vf+0xc48). It is local if it is the possessed plane with role 1 (offline). It is an enemy of the local plane if their Faction bytes differ. These replace the TODO adapter functions in E:/ACE8 PVP/mod/ProjectRVNG/Scripts/main.lua.

Hits must be carried over RVNG's own link the way Online Mode does it, shooter-authoritative. Offline the local plane is role 1, so the game refuses damage to the role-2 copy, and it refuses any damage whose attacker is the role-2 copy. On the shooter's game, catch the hit on the copy at the player-plane damage function (current 0x147D49D30, Survival's kSigPPDamage): damage, kind, attacker, weapon. Send it as RVNG's equivalent of FLiveMessageDamage {AttackerNetworkId, WeaponId, Health, Killed}. On the victim's game apply it to the victim's own plane, without the copy as instigator (refused) or through the game's damage-result path. Whether local role 3 would let the game apply hits natively is untested.

Replay the opponent's launches through the remote-fire handler (Survival T4a/T4b) and supply the missile's target, since the network-id map is empty offline. Then the copy's missile homes on the local plane and its proximity fuse and flare reaction (bIsReactiveToFlare) run natively. Its damage is refused locally (role-2 attacker), so the shooter's report is the only damage, and there is no double hit.

Mirror Online Mode's other per-event messages: PushFlare (FireFlares on the copy's weapons) and the victim's flare/cloud escapes (EscapeByFlare: PlayerMissileEscapeNum / DoubleLockonEscapeNum, EscapeInClouds) back to the shooter. Also send lock state (LockedTarget bLockOn / SelectedTarget) so the victim's plane can fill LockonAttackerPlayerPlanes / TargetingPlayerPlanes and give missile warnings. For ESM/ECM, use a role flip around the electronic update or an ElectronicMeasureEffect equivalent: the stock update skips weapons owned by role-2 planes.

Balance: for player against player, the campaign and online category damage tables are the same (attacker Fighter 110%, Multirole 100%, Attacker 85%, Electronic 100%), so RVNG need not force the online table unless NPCs take part. If RVNG wants DM rules, the stock values are VictoryScore 500000, MissionLimitTime 210 s, BaseRespawnTime 10 s and HighThreatTargetScore 900 (marks the high-threat target).

The HUD callsign online is 'Online_Hud_OnlineMissionCallsign_<Faction>_<index>_Name'. Offline RVNG can write the callsign/ObjName/gamer tag strings as Survival's SV_PPName does, but the gamer-tag line shows only in an online game mode.
blockers: The player's lock-candidate builder (TargetSelectionComponent TargetCandidates/AllyGameObjects) and the HUD box colour/ALLY-ENEMY text code are not in readable .text; they are probably in the protected .sbss section. That they use Faction / vf+0x8d8 is inferred, not read.

The exact caller and timing of 0x1471b3a00 (vtable slot +0xa70 of 0x14c7013a8, reached through a68/a70/a78 time-notification calls) is unknown. It may run again on respawn or registration and reset RVNG's factions.

CanBeDamagedBy / game-object TakeDamage addresses are from the pre-patch (2026-09-29/10-30) RE; they jump into protected code and were not re-derived for the 2026-11-02 build. Only the player-plane damage (0x147D49D30) and RemoteUpdate (0x147D5E9E0) are confirmed current from a Survival log.
The receive handlers for EscapeByFlare, LockedTarget and SelectedTarget were not found; only the message and field names are known.

Reading the Survival .env directly was refused by the permission system. Packages were extracted with the repo's own key helper (python -I tools/env.py --aes-key piped into retoc, never printed) into the scratch folder only.
openQuestions: Solo test with a COOP2MP-style role-2 copy: set the copy's Faction to 2 (Bravo), keeping the local plane at 1, through SetFaction. Does the HUD show ENEMY (red box, HUD_ColorHostile) and the minimap IconTextureRaivalPlayer? Does the copy appear in the local TargetSelectionComponent.TargetCandidates (+0x870) instead of AllyGameObjects (+0x890), and can it be locked with missiles that home on it? Log both arrays every second.

Hook SetFaction (0x147d0b980) and 0x1471b3a00 and log every call, and log both planes' +0x3b2 once a second through a full mission with a death and respawn. Does anything reset the copy to Alpha after it was set to Bravo, and when?

With factions different, fire the gun and a missile at the role-2 copy. Do the hits reach player-plane damage 0x147D49D30, and does it return 0 (role-1 attacker vs role-2 target refused)? Then set the local plane's +0xed8 to 3 and repeat: is damage applied, and does anything else switch to online behaviour (SendDamage, HUD)?

Have the copy (fed by the opponent) launch a missile at the local plane and the local pilot fire flares. Does the replayed missile divert natively (bIsReactiveToFlare)? Measure the miss rate with flares, to decide whether an EscapeByFlare-style report back to the shooter is needed.

Load OnlineMode/Maps/Dm (PL_DM_00x + WD_DM + EP_DM + MC_DM) with BP_ChronicleDeathMatchGameMode offline. Does it start without Strix (its GameStateClass/HUDClass imports)? Do the EP_DM EnemyPlayer triggers (PlayerDestroyByRank_Top, ObjectDestroy_ao) fire when the local pilot kills the Bravo copy?

missed: DEATHMATCH HAS ITS OWN NATIVE FACTION ASSIGNER. ALiveSoloPVPGameMode overrides game-mode slot +0xa30 with 0x1471e0230; ALiveDeathMatchGameMode inherits it (DM vtable 0x14c693718, LEA 0x146df1b0f; SoloPVP vtable 0x14ca32fe8). It copies CachedPlayerPlanes and sorts them with 0x1473b6430. The sort key is the uint32 at NetworkObject(+0xed0)+0x28, or 0 with no network object (null-safe comparator at 0x1473b6519-0x1473b654a). Each plane i gets default faction i+1 (Alpha..Zulu) and default name string 'ALPHA'..'ZULU' (UTF-16 constants 0x14cb3e5c0..0x14cb3e460, 8 entries, i % 8). 0x1474b6700 then overrides these only if the NetworkManager member map has the plane's +0x2200 key. SetFaction and 0x147d3f0c0 follow (0x1471e07f0-0x1471e085b). So the stock DM mode would give two offline player planes Alpha and Bravo by itself, ordered by network id. Evidence: dis 1471e0230 -> scratchpad/pvp_research/targeting-verify/fn_1471e0230.txt. Static.

Per-mode implementations of game-mode slot +0xa30 ('apply player-plane factions', current build): ALiveCampaignGameMode 0x1478dbe90 sets all Alpha, callsign empty, index 0. ALiveFreeFlightGameMode 0x1471b3a00 calls Super, then sets all Alpha if StrixManager+0x1fa==0. ALiveOnlineGameMode 0x1471c5a50 is used by Coop/CompetitiveCoop/EmergencyCall/TeamPVP/TDM/PVPVE: member map only, so a miss leaves the faction as an uninitialized stack byte. ALiveSoloPVPGameMode/DM 0x1471e0230 uses index-based defaults. Online, slot +0xa30 is called from 0x1471c6810 (online game-mode slot +0xca8). That caller is gated on NetworkManager member-state counts: 0x1474cc700(NM+0x210, 5/6) compared with 0x1474b39e0. The host path also calls 0x1474b6a60, and 0x1474ae360 and 0x1471c6150 run after. Static. This answers part of the report's 'timing unknown' blocker.

Damage acceptance uses hostility (current build). Chain: player-plane damage 0x147D49D30 -> chunk 0x147d4a061 -> game-object damage 0x147d0fde0. That calls CanBeDamagedBy stub 0x147d1a990 ('jmp 0x15c709b60', protected; skipped for damage kinds 7/8/9 at 0x147d0fe87), then 0x147d12950. 0x147d12950 requires victim +0x3f4 set, +0xdb8 clear and health > 0. If an attacker is given, IsEnemy(victim, attacker) must be true unless kind==7 or victim bCanBeDamagedByAlly(+0xb50) is set. It then checks +0x3f8/+0x3f9/+0x3fa/+0x3fb/+0x3fc flags, world AuthorityGameMode != null and damage != 0. So two same-faction pilots cannot hurt each other natively, whatever their roles. Also, delivering a hit with attacker = null skips the IsEnemy test. Static.

IsEnemy wrapper 0x147d0ba00(a, b): World = GetWorld(a); gm = World+0x158 (AuthorityGameMode), IsA-checked via 0x146dcdcf0, else null; then tail-jumps to a->vf+0x8d8(b, gm). It has 115 direct call sites (xcall.py 147d0ba00): target selection, minimap, laser interceptor, AI and weapons. Hooking or calling this wrapper is the single native place to test 'is X my enemy'. Static.

Lock-on list builder (readable, chunk 0x14728450b of ULiveTargetSelectionComponent). Per candidate it calls IsEnemy(OwningPlayerPlane +0x840, cand). Not hostile -> AllyGameObjects +0x890. Hostile -> UnTargetableCandidates +0x880 when the target is an AI with bIsNotLockonTarget (+0x117a) or fails the vf+0xae8 / comp +0x9d6/+0x9d7 gates; otherwise a working list handed to 0x1472852c0 (TargetCandidates path). Static. The minimap's ULiveMiniMapWidget (CachedPlayerPlane +0x4b0) likewise calls vf+0x8d8 at 0x1472af9cd, with the UnidentifiedType==Ally override. Static.

Online callsign keys exist in the exe only for Alpha_1..8, Bravo_1..4 and Charlie/Delta/Lima/Oscar/Romeo/Zulu _1, plus team names Online_Hud_OnlineMissionCallsign_Alpha_Name / _Bravo_Name (UTF-16 at 0x14cb3d690..0x14cbe09d0). This matches the DM layout (one pilot per faction beyond Alpha/Bravo) and the remote spawn's slot rule (Alpha idx<=8, Bravo idx+4, others slot 0). Static.

Faction is carried in Strix messages after all: FLiveMessageSetObjectInformation (serializers 0x1452505c0/0x145251300), FLiveMessageTeamScoreAddition (0x145257780/0x145257dd0: Score, PhaseIndex, ScoreType, Faction), FLiveMessageChangeBot (0x14528ac00/0x14528b690: PlayerNetworkId, BotNetworkId, AircraftId, CallSign, Weapon1-4Id, Health, Faction) and FLiveMessageOperateBot (0x14528bc60/0x14528c3b0). A player-to-bot takeover therefore keeps the leaver's faction, and team score is keyed by faction. Static (leaxref.py 14bfc7938 + strings each serializer uses).
Faction None (0) is hostile to every non-None faction under 0x147d0ba90. A plane left at the zero default would be an enemy of all Alpha allies and AI, not neutral. Static.

The network role byte +0xed8 is a native ALiveGameObject field: it sits between NetworkObject +0xed0 and TargetPinsPlayerPlanes +0xee0 (propoff LockonAttackerPlayerPlanes). AI objects carry it too (COOP2MP: AI is 3 on its host and 2 elsewhere). The remote spawn also computes a role of 2 + bool(0x1474b38d0(NM)) at 0x1471b79f3-0x1471b7a1f. Static.

ULiveGameInstance has NetworkP2P_ (ULiveNetworkP2P*) at +0x930, next to StrixManager_ +0x910, MatchmakerManager_ +0x918, StrixMessenger_ +0x920 and NetworkManager_ +0x928 (propoff NetworkManager_ neighbours). The game has its own P2P transport object, which is worth researching before RVNG adds a separate link. Static (existence only).

Ranked-play 'Regulations' exist as a UI concept: ULiveNUIMenuRankingInfoWidget has Text_RegulationsTitle and Text_Regurations_01..05, and ULiveNUICommonPreviewModeWidget has NoneRegulationTextId. Ranked restrictions are probably server-supplied, so the report's 'no PvP ban list' covers client tables only. Static.
